title: Buzz runtime anchor rebuild fails on custom/draft user-state links; running-app check misses buzz-desktop
body:
## Problem

Buzz interactive agents keep running an old pinned runtime because the runtime anchor can no longer be rebuilt.

- Since GH#34088 (2026-10-09), `setup.sh` links `~/.aidevops/agents/custom` and `draft` to stable user state with absolute symlinks.
- `materialize_pinned_runtime` copies the agents tree with `symlinks=True`, then `hash_runtime_tree` rejects absolute links: `team-interface-buzz-runtime: runtime source contains an absolute symbolic link`.
- Result: `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --runtime interactive` fails, so the Buzz harness stays pinned to an older anchor. On one install that anchor dated from 2026-08-10, with OpenAI-first routing. Its agent failed every turn with "The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account", even though current routing (and the custom override) are Anthropic-first.

A second gap on the same path: `buzz_is_running()` checks only `pgrep -x Buzz`. Buzz Desktop 0.5.x runs as `buzz-desktop`, so the "quit Buzz first" safety check passes while the installed app is open. `buzz-desktop-helper.sh` `_buzz_is_running` already checks both names.

## Fix

- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_agents.py`: skip top-level `custom`/`draft` links in the copy, then snapshot their resolved contents as real directories inside the anchor. Custom routing overrides apply and the anchor stays immutable.
- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py`: `buzz_is_running()` checks `Buzz` and `buzz-desktop`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs`: add linked `custom`/`draft` fixtures to the existing deployed-materialization case.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_agents.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs`

## Verification

- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs` passes. Without the agents fix, the new fixture fails with "runtime source contains an absolute symbolic link".
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-installed-startup.mjs` passes.
- After deploy: quit Buzz, run `python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --runtime interactive --project-root <registered repo> --replace`, then confirm the agent's `opencode.log` streams an `anthropic/` model.

title: planning-commit-helper.sh cannot publish task-ID normalization: rename deletions dropped and manifest refuses rows without ref:GH#
body:
## Observed

Publishing a task-ID normalization change (`task-id-normalize-helper.sh --apply`: TODO.md + todo/PLANS.md rewrites and 110 staged `git mv` brief renames) through `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: ..."` on a repo whose default branch is protected failed in two ways:

1. **Rename deletions are dropped from the publication path set.** With the renames staged, every path lister returned only the 110 destination names and none of the 110 old `todo/tasks/t0*-brief.md` paths. If publication had proceeded, the planning commit would have added the new briefs and kept the old ones (duplicate briefs for every task).
2. **The PR fallback refuses the change outright:** `Planning publication cannot safely map t13: expected one same-repository ref:GH#NNN field, found 0.` and then `Planning PR fallback failed: changed task/issue manifest is ambiguous`. Most renamed rows are old completed tasks that predate issue sync and have no `ref:GH#`, and one renamed ID appears on two rows. There is no way to publish a bulk metadata/normalization change through the helper.

The workaround was a normal branch PR with the same commit message.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh` `_planning_publish_changed_paths()` (L81-89), `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` `_todo_changed_planning_files()` (L247-259) and `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` `list_planning_changes()`/`has_planning_changes()` use `git diff --name-only` without `--no-renames`. With `diff.renames` defaulting to true, a staged rename lists only the destination, so `_todo_copy_planning_changes_to_worktree()` (L342-359) never deletes the source path in the disposable planning worktree, and `_planning_publish_snapshot()` never emits a `delete` row. Unstaged deletions (`git reset`) happen to work, which hides the bug.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` `_todo_changed_task_manifest()` (L282-319) treats every task row whose line changed (`_todo_changed_task_ids()`, L261-280, takes any `+` task line in the TODO.md diff) as a task being published, requiring exactly one current row and exactly one `ref:GH#`. A pure ID/metadata rewrite of historical rows is not a task publication.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `--no-renames` to every `git diff --name-only` used to collect planning paths (publisher, shared-todo-commit, planning-commit-helper), so a rename yields a source delete plus a destination add.
2. Restrict the manifest to rows that are new or changed in status/ref (or accept an explicit metadata-only mode, e.g. `AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_METADATA_ONLY=1`, whose PR body carries no task markers), so bulk normalization can publish through the helper with an empty manifest, as other metadata-only planning PRs already do.

## Verification

- Fixture repo with a protected-branch stub (`AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_FORCE_PR_FALLBACK=1`): stage `git mv todo/tasks/t038.21-brief.md todo/tasks/t38.21-brief.md` plus a TODO.md task-line rewrite on a completed row without `ref:GH#`. `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: normalize"` creates a planning PR whose diff deletes the old brief and adds the new one.
- `_todo_changed_planning_files` and `_planning_publish_changed_paths` list both rename source and destination with the renames staged.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: task-id-normalize-helper.sh leaves BRIEF: continuation paths and alpha-suffixed legacy rows unnormalized
body:
## Observed

Running `task-id-normalize-helper.sh --apply` on a managed repo with ~325 padded legacy task rows (no CONFLICT lines in `--dry-run`) left two gaps. Relationship sync still could not build the graph until they were fixed by hand:

1. **Indented `BRIEF:` continuation lines are not rewritten.** The helper renamed 110 `todo/tasks/t0*-brief.md` files, but 89 indented continuation lines (`  BRIEF: todo/tasks/t038.21-brief.md`) under task rows still pointed at the old filenames. Every one dangled after `--apply`, and `--advisory` still printed nothing.
2. **Alpha-suffixed legacy IDs (`t038.36a`) are skipped, and the graph builder then aborts on them.** `unpad()` only matches `t0+[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*`, so `t038.36a` is left as is. When such a completed `[x]` row carries any `blocked-by:`/`blocks:` value, `issue-sync-helper.sh relationships` fails with `Cannot build a complete TODO dependency graph`.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/task-id-normalize-helper.sh` `active_lines()` (~L57-100) marks only task lines (`task_line` regex, L42) as active in `TODO.md`. Continuation lines are yielded inactive, so `brief_ref.sub(...)` (L135) never sees indented `BRIEF:` fields. `--advisory` uses the same filter (L115), so it cannot warn about them either.
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh` `_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row()` (L349-369) returns 1 for any ID failing `^t[0-9]{1,18}(\.[0-9]{1,18}){0,8}$` (L354). `_relationship_declared_edges()` (L407) accepts alpha segments (`\.[0-9a-z]+`), so an alpha-suffixed completed row reaches the skip function and always aborts the whole graph. Completed rows that merely *reference* such IDs are skipped by `_relationship_report_parse_failure()` (L390-392), which is inconsistent.

## Proposed fix

1. In the normalize helper, treat indented continuation lines that belong to an active task row (at least `BRIEF:` fields) as active for `brief_ref` rewriting, and include them in `--advisory`. After `--apply`, verify that every rewritten `todo/tasks/*-brief.md` reference exists, and fail loudly otherwise.
2. Either report alpha-suffixed padded IDs as a CONFLICT/manual item in `--dry-run` (there is no canonical form), or let `_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row()` skip completed alpha-suffixed rows whose dependencies do not touch active work, as it already does for numeric legacy rows.

## Verification

- Fixture TODO.md with a padded task row plus an indented `BRIEF: todo/tasks/t038.21-brief.md` line: `--apply` renames the brief and rewrites the continuation path; `--advisory` warns before `--apply`.
- Fixture with a completed `- [x] t038.36a ... blocked-by:t038.33` row: `--dry-run` lists it, and `issue-sync-helper.sh relationships <other-task>` no longer prints `Cannot build a complete TODO dependency graph`.

title: Primary/remote-interactive sessions: fail over on definite model entitlement rejection instead of retrying
body:
## Problem

A Buzz remote-interactive agent whose primary model is rejected before generation retries the same model for about 22 minutes, then posts a generic error.

## Reproducer

Observed 2026-11-07 on Buzz Desktop 0.5.28 with an aidevops interactive agent.

1. The agent's primary model resolved to `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, and the ChatGPT OAuth account does not have that model.
2. The user sends "hello" at 02:05.
3. `opencode.log` for the agent shows the same request at 02:06:17, 02:06:23, 02:06:34, 02:06:52, 02:07:27, 02:08:41 and 02:11:01. Each one fails with `AI_APICallError: The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.`
4. The chat shows only typing dots until 02:28, when Buzz posts: "I couldn't process the last request after multiple retries (Agent reported error (code -32603): Internal error: The 'gpt-5.6-sol' model is not supported ...)".

The rejection is definite and pre-generation, so retrying the same model cannot succeed.

## Expected

- The aidevops plugin treats a definite entitlement rejection in a primary or remote-interactive session the way GH#36698 treats a child session: mark the model unavailable for this auth, then continue on the next connected candidate in the same routing tier. It never picks a lower tier or a model outside the routing table.
- If no candidate is left, fail once with a clear message naming the rejected model and the next step (re-authenticate or change routing), instead of letting the client retry.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-entitlement-failover.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-unavailability.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/specialist-advisor.mjs`
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/primary-entitlement-failover.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs`

Integration evidence: `index.mjs` already wires `createSubagentEffortHooks` into `chat.message`, `chat.params` and `event`. Compose root-session recovery in that factory rather than add another independent index hook. Its current lifecycle recovery only handles child Task sessions. The existing test file contains the GH#36698 cases requested below. Collision discovery found no related open PR or competing claim for these paths. Verify with `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs` and existing routing/specialist tests. This correction does not change the outcome or exclusions.

Notes:

- `subagent-entitlement-failover.mjs` is the reference pattern (GH#36698 child failover). Reuse its candidate walk and the `model-unavailability.mjs` marking.
- `applyDailyDriverDefaults` in `specialist-advisor.mjs` is where the primary model default comes from.
- The hook that receives primary-session errors is not known yet. Start with `rg -n "session.error|entitlement" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`.

## Out of scope

Buzz's own client-side retry of a non-retryable `-32603` error is upstream behaviour (block/buzz-app). If needed, file it there separately with this reproducer.

## Verification

- Extend the existing GH#36698 failover tests (`rg -l "36698" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests`) with a primary-session case: the first candidate is rejected, the session continues on the next candidate, and the rejected model is not retried within the TTL.
- `node --test` on the touched plugin test files passes.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: issue-sync relationships: #32313 follow-up - one graph build still takes 83-87 s of the 90 s budget (parse_task_line per dependency row), so the broad pass never completes a task
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #32313 / PR #32318. On a history-heavy `TODO.md`, the hosted Issue Sync relationship pass still makes no progress. Building the dependency graph once (the #32318 change) takes **83-87 s of the 90 s default budget**. About 3 s remain for mutations, so the pass defers every task on every run.

The cost is in one place. `_relationship_declared_edges` calls the general-purpose `parse_task_line` for every row carrying `blocked-by:`/`blocks:`, including completed history, but uses only 2 of its 16 fields. Each call creates 72 processes and takes about 61 ms. A prototype that keeps the same filters and failure rules but parses in-process builds the **identical edge set in 1.46 s instead of 83.4 s** (see below).

Please do not fix this by raising the deadline. #32313 asked for that explicitly, and the workflow does not need it once the build is cheap.

## What #32318 fixed and what remains

- #32313 measured this same function at 109.54 s on this ledger and asked that "repeated invocations do not rescan thousands of completed rows per edge" and that a history-heavy fixture "makes measurable progress under its documented budget".
- #32318 fixed the repetition. The graph is now built once per pass (`_relationship_prepare_edge_snapshot`) and reused for cycle checks. It did not reduce the cost of that single build, which alone uses up the budget.
- The #32318 benchmark did not catch this. In `tests/benchmark-issue-sync-relationships.sh` (L88-107) the 800 history rows are `- [x] tN completed history`, with **no** `blocked-by:`/`blocks:`. They are filtered out before `parse_task_line`, so only 2 rows are parsed, and that section asserts edge correctness, not elapsed time. In real ledgers, completed rows usually keep their dependency metadata.

Related history: #27849 (aggregate deadline), #28945 (resumable progress), #29968 (targeted sync), #30020 / PR #30079 (hosted resume state).

## Evidence

The consumer repo is private, so its identity is withheld. All measurements are read-only, with no GitHub writes.

### Hosted run on current code (`ref: main`, 2026-11-07)

Step: `issue-sync-helper.sh relationships --verbose` from `issue-sync-reusable.yml` (L390-405), self-hosted Linux runner:

```text
Syncing relationships for 30 task(s) in <private-repo> (pending: 30, resume: fresh)   # logged 87 s after step start
Edges: created=0 already-present=0 failed=0 deferred=3
Tasks: attempted=1 complete=0/30 | Retryable: 3 | Deadline exhausted: true
Timing: parse=87s mutation=3s | Backend calls: 2
Failure: deferred:deadline
```

Earlier context: hosted runs pinned to v3.34.12 (before #32318), from 2026-09-24 to 2026-10-06, all ended `complete=0/26` or `2/28` with `mutation=128-160s`. Between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-06 the graph build aborted on legacy padded task IDs. The consumer has since normalized those, so the build now succeeds and this budget problem is visible again.

### Local profile of the same ledger

Framework scripts were byte-identical to `marcusquinn/aidevops` `main` @ `79f4638`.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Ledger | 5,344 lines; 1,843 task rows |
| Rows with `blocked-by:`/`blocks:` | 1,111 (1,083 completed/declined, 28 open) |
| Unique declared edges | 2,341 |
| `strip_code_fences` | 15 ms |
| `_relationship_active_ids_and_refs` (already scans every row for the same two fields, in-process) | 204 ms |
| `parse_task_line`, per call | **61 ms** (mean of 50) |
| `parse_task_line`, processes per call (strace) | **72 fork/clone, 26 exec**: `sed` ×19, `grep` ×5, `tr` ×2 |
| `task_identity_validate`, per call (subshell) | 3 ms |
| `_relationship_declared_edges`, total | **83.4-85.7 s** |

1,111 rows × about 61 ms accounts for most of the total. The rest is per-reference validation subshells.

## Root cause (file:line on main @ 79f4638)

1. `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh:399-440` (`_relationship_declared_edges`) runs `parsed=$(parse_task_line "$task_line")` (L413) for every dependency-bearing row, then reads only `blocked_by` and `blocks` from the result.
2. `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh:350-442` (`parse_task_line`) extracts 16 fields through chains of `echo | grep/sed/tr` pipelines inside command substitutions. Its dependency helpers (`_task_dependency_value` L270-302, `_task_parent_value` L304-328, `_task_id_from_todo_line` L175-188) validate each ID with `task_identity_validate`, which runs `task_identity_parse` in a subshell (`.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh:87-94`).
3. `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:164-184` starts the aggregate deadline before workset preparation and the graph build. `issue-sync-relationships-state.sh:346-355` sets the default to 90 s, so build time is charged to the mutation budget.

The broad workset is already limited to open and in-progress rows (`issue-sync-relationships-sync.sh:452`, 30 tasks here). Mutation work is small. The graph build dominates.

## Prototype (evidence, not a PR)

It is a drop-in replacement for the `_relationship_declared_edges` loop with the same row filter, the same legacy-row handling (`_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row`) and the same failure reporting (`_relationship_report_parse_failure`). Parsing is done with Bash regex and no subshells per row. It mirrors:

- `task_identity_parse`'s legacy and namespaced EREs and `TASK_IDENTITY_MAX_BYTES`
- `_task_dependency_value`'s separator rules, `(GH)?#N` skip and per-reference validation
- `_task_parent_value`'s duplicate/invalid `parent:` rejection
- `_task_id_from_todo_line`'s checkbox set (`[ x>-]`)

Results:

- **Real ledger:** 1.46 s against 83.4 s for the stock builder, with an identical sorted edge set (2,341 edges, empty diff). A version that still used `$(...)` for the two dependency lookups took 5.75 s, so per-row subshells are the main remaining cost.
- **Edge-case fixture:** identical 8-edge sets. Both builders skip completed rows with a trailing comma (`blocked-by:t15,`), an uppercase `[X]` checkbox, or duplicate `parent:`. Both drop self-references and `GH#5` refs, emit `blocks:` from a declined `[-]` row, and exclude fenced code.
- **Fail-closed fixture:** an open row with `blocked-by:t025` makes **both** builders exit 1, so "Cannot build a complete TODO dependency graph" behaviour is preserved.

<details><summary>Prototype functions (Bash)</summary>

```bash
# Pure-Bash equivalent of task_identity_validate (no subshell).
_fast_task_id_valid() {
	local input="$1"
	local legacy_ere='^t[1-9][0-9]{0,17}(\.[1-9][0-9]{0,17}){0,8}$'
	local namespaced_ere='^to[0-7][0-9a-hjkmnp-tv-z]{25}-[1-9][0-9]{0,17}(\.[1-9][0-9]{0,17}){0,8}$'
	[[ -n "$input" && "${#input}" -le "${TASK_IDENTITY_MAX_BYTES:-199}" ]] || return 1
	[[ "$input" =~ $legacy_ere || "$input" =~ $namespaced_ere ]] && return 0
	return 1
}

# Mirrors _task_dependency_value; result in _FAST_DEP_OUT, return 1 = row rejected.
_fast_dependency_value() {
	local line="$1" key="$2"
	local value="" dependency="" out=""
	if [[ "$line" =~ (^|[[:space:]])${key}:([^[:space:]]+) ]]; then
		value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
	fi
	[[ -n "$value" ]] || return 0
	[[ "$value" != ,* && "$value" != *, && "$value" != *,,* ]] || return 1
	local IFS=','
	for dependency in $value; do
		[[ "$dependency" =~ ^(GH)?#[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] && continue
		_fast_task_id_valid "$dependency" || return 1
		out="${out:+${out},}${dependency}"
	done
	_FAST_DEP_OUT="$out"
	return 0
}

# Mirrors _task_parent_value failure rules (duplicate or invalid parent:).
_fast_parent_ok() {
	local line="$1"
	local matched="" value="" remainder=""
	[[ "$line" =~ (^|[[:space:]])parent:([^[:space:]]+) ]] || return 0
	matched="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
	value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
	remainder="${line#*"$matched"}"
	[[ ! "$remainder" =~ (^|[[:space:]])parent: ]] || return 1
	[[ "$value" =~ ^GH#[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] && return 0
	_fast_task_id_valid "$value" || return 1
	return 0
}

_fast_declared_edges() {
	local todo_file="$1"
	local stripped="" task_line="" task_id="" blocked_by="" blocks="" dep="" checkbox=""
	stripped=$(strip_code_fences <"$todo_file") || return 1
	_relationship_active_ids_and_refs "$stripped" || return 1
	while IFS= read -r task_line; do
		[[ "$task_line" == *"blocked-by:"* || "$task_line" == *"blocks:"* ]] || continue
		[[ "$task_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]+\[(.)\][[:space:]]+(t[0-9]+(\.[0-9a-z]+)*)[[:space:]] ]] || continue
		checkbox="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
		task_id="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
		if ! _fast_task_id_valid "$task_id"; then
			_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row "$task_line" "$task_id" || return 1
			continue
		fi
		_FAST_DEP_OUT=""
		if [[ "$checkbox" != [[:space:]x\>-] ]] || ! _fast_parent_ok "$task_line" ||
			! _fast_dependency_value "$task_line" blocked-by; then
			_relationship_report_parse_failure "$task_line" "$task_id" || return 1
			continue
		fi
		blocked_by="$_FAST_DEP_OUT"
		_FAST_DEP_OUT=""
		if ! _fast_dependency_value "$task_line" blocks; then
			_relationship_report_parse_failure "$task_line" "$task_id" || return 1
			continue
		fi
		blocks="$_FAST_DEP_OUT"
		local IFS=','
		for dep in $blocked_by; do
			[[ -n "$dep" && "$dep" != "$task_id" ]] && printf '%s|%s\n' "$task_id" "$dep"
		done
		for dep in $blocks; do
			[[ -n "$dep" && "$dep" != "$task_id" ]] && printf '%s|%s\n' "$dep" "$task_id"
		done
		unset IFS
	done <<<"$stripped"
	return 0
}
```

This is prototype quality. A real change should share the ERE with `task-identity-lib.sh` rather than duplicate it, and should restore `IFS` handling to the codebase's conventions.

</details>

## Proposed fix

**Primary (narrow):** in `_relationship_declared_edges`, replace the per-row `parse_task_line` call with an in-process extractor for `blocked-by:`/`blocks:` (and the `parent:` validity check that currently rejects rows). It should use the same validation rules and spawn no subshells or processes per row. Expose a fork-free ID validator from `task-identity-lib.sh`, for example a `task_identity_is_valid` that matches the EREs without a subshell, so the rules stay in one place.

**Alternative (broader):** make `parse_task_line` itself fork-free. Every caller would benefit (`issue-sync-helper.sh:274,355`, `planning-publication-reconcile.sh:159,196`, `issue-sync-relationships-sync.sh:204,336`, `issue-sync-lib-compose.sh:695`), but all 16 fields have to keep exact output parity. Those callers are per task, not per row, so they are not hot paths today.

**Do not:** raise `AIDEVOPS_RELATIONSHIP_SYNC_TIMEOUT`, or set it in `issue-sync-reusable.yml`.

**Optional, maintainer's choice:** start the mutation deadline after the snapshot is built (`issue-sync-relationships.sh:164-184`), or give the build its own small bound. Once the build takes 1-2 s this matters much less.

**Open question, not needed for this fix:** whether unchanged completed rows need to be in the cycle-check graph at all.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh`: `_relationship_declared_edges` (L399-440)
- EDIT, if adding a shared validator: `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` (`task_identity_parse` L69-85, `task_identity_validate` L87-94)
- READ for semantics to mirror: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh` (L175-188, L270-328, L350-442)
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/benchmark-issue-sync-relationships.sh` (L88-107): give about 1,100 completed history rows `blocked-by:` metadata, compare the edge set with the stock builder's output, and assert a time bound on the build
- OPTIONAL `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh` (L164-184)

## Acceptance criteria

- On a synthetic ledger of at least 1,800 task rows, with at least 1,000 completed rows carrying `blocked-by:`/`blocks:`, `_relationship_declared_edges` finishes in **under 10 s** on CI (about 85 s today). Its sorted output must match the current implementation's exactly.
- Failure behaviour is unchanged:
  - Open rows with invalid refs, bad separators, or duplicate/invalid `parent:` still make the graph build fail.
  - Unparseable completed rows are still skipped with the INFO line.
  - Legacy padded completed rows follow `_relationship_skip_completed_legacy_row`.
  - Fenced code stays excluded.
- On such a ledger with the default 90 s budget, the broad pass reports single-digit `Timing: parse=`, attempts more than 1 task, and carries the remainder through the existing resume state.
- No change to `AIDEVOPS_RELATIONSHIP_SYNC_TIMEOUT` defaults or workflow env.

title: fix(review-bot-gate): private org members classified external in status-json evidence, final merge trust gate blocks PASS_RATE_LIMITED PRs
body:
## What

The deterministic merge pass blocks every `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` (and `PASS_ADVISORY` / `SKIP`) PR whose author is a **private** org member with admin/write permission. The final trust gate requires `author.class == "trusted"`. `review-bot-gate-helper.sh status-json` derives that class only from the REST `author_association`, and GitHub reports private org members there as `CONTRIBUTOR`.

This is a sibling of the private-org-member fixes in GH#34644, GH#34703, GH#34875, GH#35355, GH#35569 and GH#35622. Those added a collaborator-permission fallback to dispatch, claim, linked-issue and terminal-blocker trust. The review-gate evidence path has no such fallback.

## Evidence (2026-11-07, v3.39.131, managed private-org repo)

- `review-bot-gate-helper.sh status-json <PR> <slug>` on a runner-authored worker PR returns `"status":"PASS_RATE_LIMITED","author":{"association":"CONTRIBUTOR","class":"external"},"permitted":true,"reason":"external_rate_limit_grace","merge_gate":"clear"`.
- Same author, same PR: `gh api repos/<slug>/collaborators/<login>/permission` reports `admin`, and GraphQL `pullRequest.authorAssociation` reports `MEMBER`. REST `pulls/<n>.author_association` reports `CONTRIBUTOR`.
- `pulse.log` lists 13 distinct PRs with `final trust gate: current-head review evidence is PASS_RATE_LIMITED or unpermitted ... merge blocked`. They are APPROVED and MERGEABLE, and they keep a per-repo open-PR backlog guardrail tripped (`open_prs_counted=23 threshold=20`), which suppresses about 90 ordinary dispatch candidates.
- Main still has the strict gate: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:1034-1054` (`_pmrc_review_evidence_permits_advisory`).

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` `do_status_json` (~line 1889), when the REST association is not OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, fall back to `gh api repos/<repo>/collaborators/<author_login>/permission`. Classify `admin|maintain|write` as `$RBG_AUTHOR_CLASS_TRUSTED`, and fail closed on any API error. Reuse whichever permission-fallback helper GH#34644 / GH#35622 introduced instead of writing a new one. Find it with `rg -n "collaborators/.*permission" .agents/scripts/`.
2. Mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Keep GH#17671 defence-in-depth: login, labels or runner identity alone must never grant trust; only the live permission API may.
3. Leave `_pmrc_review_evidence_permits_advisory` unchanged. It should start passing once the evidence class is correct.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-status.sh` (do_status_json moved here by GH#37011; author class derivation lives here)
- EDIT (only if the shared fallback helper needs exporting): the lib that hosts the GH#34644 permission fallback (path not verified, find it with `rg`)

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` reports zero violations.
- `review-bot-gate-helper.sh status-json <PR> <slug>` for a private-member admin author reports `"class":"trusted"`. For a genuinely external author (permission `read`/`none`/404) it still reports `"external"`.
- On the next pulse cycle, `rg "final trust gate" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` stops listing those PRs, and they merge through the normal deterministic path.

## Acceptance

- Private-org members with write+ permission get `author.class=trusted` in review-gate evidence.
- External authors stay `external`, and their merges still need exact-head maintainer crypto approval.

title: worktree-helper remove: caller session self-binds to target generation and blocks retirement (waiting-for-runs)
body:
## Summary

`worktree-helper.sh remove <path> --force` on a worktree whose registered owner PIDs are dead still refuses retirement with `status=waiting-for-runs unfinished_runs=1`. The blocking "unfinished run" is the interactive session that invoked `remove` itself: the lifecycle registry binds the caller's PID to the target generation on the first `remove` attempt, then `reconcile` observes that PID as `identity-matched/alive` and treats it as an owner.

## Evidence

- Target worktrees: two headless `--auto` workers (task `post-merge-cleanup`) killed with SIGTERM; `worktree-helper.sh registry list` shows their PIDs as `dead`.
- `worker-registry.py ... prepare-cleanup --path <wt>` → `{"status":"waiting-for-runs","unfinished_runs":1,"registered_runs":6}`.
- `registry.sqlite3` `runs` joined to `bindings` for that generation: the only `state='bound'` run has `identity.pid` equal to the interactive OpenCode session running the `remove` command (`opencode --auto --agent Build+ --tabby-shell`, cwd = the canonical repo, not the worktree).
- `events` table: at the exact timestamp of the first `remove` call, three events were appended: `expected_path` enrol, identity register (caller PID), and `{"type":"bind","run_id":...,"generation_id":...}`.
- `registry prune` reports 0 pruned; `reconcile` reports `observe-only`, nothing retired.

## Expected

A caller that only requests retirement must not become a bound owner of the generation it is retiring, or the retirement path must exclude the invoking run from the `unfinished_runs` count. Otherwise interactive `remove` can never succeed while the caller is alive, and `--force` cannot override (`--force cannot override lifecycle registry checks`).

## Files to inspect

- `worker-lifecycle/worker-registry.py` (`cleanup-worktree` / `prepare-cleanup` run registration and bind)
- `scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh` `worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree`
- `scripts/worktree-helper.sh` `remove` path

## Verification

1. Kill a headless worker owning a linked worktree.
2. From an interactive session run `worktree-helper.sh remove <path> --force` twice.
3. Expect retirement on the first or second call; currently both refuse with the caller's own PID as the sole bound run.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Required-contexts read still fails closed after GH#36866: real _gh_with_timeout path returns unclassifiable classic-protection 404
body:
## What

GH#36866 is closed and its fix is deployed, but the bug is still there. On a private managed product repo, the merge pass still fails closed on every green worker PR. The repo's default branch has no classic branch protection; its required checks come only from a repository ruleset.

The deployed `_required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached` now matches `HTTP 404|Not Found|Branch not protected|"status":"404"`, yet the production log still takes the generic `else` branch:

```
[pulse-merge] _required_contexts_for_default_branch: branch protection API failed for <repo> (exit 1) — caller will fail closed (t2922)
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #N in <repo> — REST required checks could not be classified (t3567)
```

So the text that reaches `protection_resp` through the real `_pmrc_gh_read` → `_gh_with_timeout read` path does not contain the 404 markers. The GH#36866 regression test mocks the raw `gh` binary inside the unit under test, so it never runs the real transport, cooldown, or shim layers. That is why it passed while production still fails.

## Evidence (supervisor pulse, 2026-11-07 ~05:30Z, runner on aidevops v3.39.x)

- The deployed `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` (mtime 2026-11-06 02:01Z) contains the GH#36866 grep at about lines 334-340.
- `rg -c "branch protection API failed for <repo>" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` returns 1922. The occurrences continue through 2026-11-07T05:30Z, about 27h after the fix was deployed.
- A direct `gh api repos/<repo>/branches/<default>/protection/required_status_checks` returns the body `{"message":"Branch not protected",...,"status":"404"}` and the stderr `gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)`. The runner account has `admin`.
- `gh api repos/<repo>/rules/branches/<default>` returns one `required_status_checks` ruleset (Format, Lint, Typecheck, Unit Tests), so the GH#34965 fallback plus the ruleset merge would resolve the contexts correctly if the 404 were classified.
- Side effect that wastes CI: right after each fail-closed skip, the CI-drift path logs `CI-drift context classification unavailable ... allowing one rebase` → `required-check head-state unavailable before CI-drift update-branch; fail-open to existing update-branch behaviour (GH#26406)` → `CI-drift rebase succeeded via update-branch`. This repeats on every merge cycle for about 20 worker PRs that already passed all gates and had a PASS/PASS_RATE_LIMITED review gate. CI keeps re-running and nothing merges.

## Where

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`: `_required_contexts_for_default_branch_uncached` (classic read about lines 325-370) and `_pmrc_gh_read` (about line 44).
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`: `_gh_with_timeout` (about line 605), `_gh_timeout_cooldown_preflight`, `_gh_record_cooldown_response_if_needed`, `_gh_replay_transport_output`. Also check the `.agents/scripts/gh` PATH shim and any REST quota/route-decision layer reached via `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_COST=1 AIDEVOPS_GH_ROUTE_DECISION=pulse-branch-protection-required-contexts-rest`.
- Test: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh` (the GH#36866 case at about lines 247-255 and 1110-1134 stubs `gh` directly).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-phantom-pending-checks.sh`

Integration scope note (worker, GH#37026): the fix makes any non-deferral classic-settings read failure fall back to the readable branch metadata endpoint, so it no longer depends on matching 404 text. `test-pulse-merge-phantom-pending-checks.sh::test_branch_protection_api_error` asserted the old contract (generic settings error fails closed even when branch metadata proves the branch is unprotected). Its mock must make the branch metadata read fail too, so it keeps testing the fail-closed path.

## Likely cause (unverified, confirm first)

One of these returns exit 1 with text that has no 404 marker:

- a cooldown recorded after an earlier 404 makes `_gh_timeout_cooldown_preflight` short-circuit later reads,
- the REST quota/route governor rejects the read,
- the PATH shim rewrites the error.

## How

1. Reproduce through the real stack. Source `shared-constants.sh` and `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, then put a stub `gh` executable on PATH that prints the JSON body on stdout and `gh: Branch not protected (HTTP 404)` on stderr and exits 1. Call `_pmrc_gh_read gh api repos/o/r/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks 2>&1` twice in a row and print exactly what comes back each time. The second call matters because it exposes cooldown or governor effects.
2. Fix the layer that drops or replaces the 404, so a terminal HTTP 404 on a read reaches the caller unchanged and is never recorded as a retryable cooldown. If a governor refusal is the cause, make it distinguishable: a refusal should be a local deferral (`_pmrc_emit_local_deferral`) and must not be logged as "branch protection API failed".
3. Make the GH#36866 regression test exercise `_gh_with_timeout` (do not stub `_pmrc_gh_read`), and run the call twice.
4. Optional, if it stays small: the CI-drift path should not `update-branch` the same unchanged head again on every cycle when the required-context classification is unavailable. Rebase at most once per head. Otherwise split this into a follow-up issue.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh` passes, including the new real-transport 404 case.
- `shellcheck` reports zero issues on the changed files.
- After deploy, `rg -c "branch protection API failed for <repo>" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` stops growing, `active rulesets add required contexts` appears for that repo, and gated green worker PRs merge.

Ref #36866

title: CI-drift: rebase at most once per head when required-context classification is unavailable
body:
## What

When required-context classification is unavailable, the merge pass rebases the same unchanged PR head on every cycle. Make it rebase at most once per head.

Split from #37026, step 4 of its "How" section. That issue fixes the classification failure. This one removes the wasted CI it caused.

## Why

`_pmp_stage_required_checks` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (about lines 1413-1432) computes `drift_signature` only when `_required_checks_terminal_failure_names` succeeds. When classification is unavailable, it logs `CI-drift context classification unavailable ... allowing one rebase` and leaves `drift_signature` empty. The ledger check `_ci_drift_ledger_should_skip` and `_ci_drift_ledger_record` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-ci-drift-ledger.sh`) both run only when the signature is non-empty. So "allowing one rebase" actually allows one rebase per cycle. In the #37026 incident, about 20 green worker PRs got `update-branch` on every merge cycle, CI re-ran each time, and nothing merged.

## How

1. In `_pmp_stage_required_checks`, when classification is unavailable, set `drift_signature` to a fixed sentinel such as `classification-unavailable`. The existing ledger skip and record calls then cover it, keyed on the current `pr_head_ref_oid`.
2. Once a skip happens, the existing path routes the PR to a CI fix-worker. Check whether that is right when classification is unavailable; it probably is not, because no failing check is known. If it is not, return 1 and wait for the next cycle with no rebase and no routing. Log the choice.
3. Keep `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` unchanged unless the head-state guard needs the same sentinel.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-cases.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-ci-drift-ledger.sh`

Brief repaired: #37037 moved the existing ledger-routing cases into the sibling cases module. The ledger validates hexadecimal signatures and deliberately skips different heads for known failures; unavailable classification needs a hashed sentinel plus an explicit same-head comparison, preserving known-failure behavior. Collision discovery found no open related PR. Verify with the existing routing suite and ShellCheck on all changed shell files.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` passes. If it is cheap, add a case: classification unavailable twice on the same head gives one rebase, then a skip.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` reports zero findings.
- After deploy, `CI-drift rebase succeeded via update-branch` appears at most once per PR head in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` while classification stays unavailable.

Ref #37026

title: fix(lifecycle): automatic cleanup never retires stale modern-generation worktrees (managed-by-current-cleanup)
body:
## What

Make automatic worktree cleanup actually retire stale **modern-generation** worktrees (registry entries with `modern=True`) that are clean, pushed and idle. Today they are retained forever with reason `managed-by-current-cleanup`.

## Why

Read-only preview of the automatic cleanup pass on a real host (registry with 1509 entries): **1051 retained as `managed-by-current-cleanup`**, 4 eligible, 0 attempted. Registry event census on two hosts: 0 `reconstructible-*` events ever; only operator-confirmed legacy retirements happened. Disk filled to 94% before manual cleanup. Ref #36626 (the `--ignored` cause was fixed in #37025; this is the second cause).

## Evidence / suspected causes (verify each)

1. `worker_lifecycle/legacy_options.py:71` `require_managed_takeover` converts **every** guard failure (`ValueError`, `OSError`, `SubprocessError`, `ObservationUnavailable`) into `managed-by-current-cleanup`, so the real blocking guard is invisible. First step: preserve the underlying reason (e.g. `managed-by-current-cleanup` as status + `violation`/`detail` = original reason) so the preview reports why.
2. `worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py:183-200` `process_item` calls `require_confirmation` (manual-authority check, line 48) **before** the `item["modern"]` branch. Verify whether this blocks unattended takeover for unconfirmed paths; takeover of modern generations must not require `--confirm-legacy-path`.
3. `worker_lifecycle/legacy_inventory.py:114` `inspect` raises `managed-by-current-cleanup` for any modern item; check whether any automatic path reaches `take_over_managed` (`legacy_cleanup.py:168`) at all.
4. One pass examines only 25 registry entries; with >1000 stale entries convergence takes many passes. Check the cap and whether retained entries are re-examined first (starvation).
5. Many entries may belong to registry generations without runs / already-absent paths; those should reconcile to absent, not stay retained.

## Reproducer

On a host with an existing lifecycle registry (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worker-lifecycle/registry.sqlite3`) holding stale modern-generation entries, run the automatic legacy cleanup pass in preview mode (no `--apply`, no `--confirm-legacy-path`) and tally `status`/`reason` per item. Observed: 1509 examined, 1051 `managed-by-current-cleanup`, 0 attempted. Registry `events` table contains no `reconstructible-*` event types.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_options.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_inventory.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_legacy_cleanup.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`


- Files: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_options.py`, `legacy_cleanup.py`, `legacy_inventory.py`; docs `.agents/worker-lifecycle/LEGACY-CLEANUP.md`.
- Pattern: `process_reconstructible` / `reconstructible(..., managed=True)` already implement the safety guards (clean incl. untracked, idle `/proc` census, unlocked, HEAD on remote ref, no open PR, non-forced removal, branch kept). Keep those guards; fix reporting and reachability.
- Do not weaken: unpushed/dirty/locked/in-use/open-PR worktrees must stay retained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Preview output of the automatic pass shows the concrete guard reason for each retained modern entry.
- A clean, pushed, idle, unlocked modern worktree older than the age threshold with no open PR is retired by the automatic (unconfirmed) pass, with archive/receipt as for reconstructible retirement.
- Dirty / unpushed / in-use / open-PR modern worktrees are still retained.
- Existing suite passes: `cd .agents/worker-lifecycle && umask 022 && python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests` (also under `umask 002` once #37027 lands).

## Verification

Run the suite above; add focused tests only for the changed decision paths (unconfirmed modern takeover allowed when guards hold; reason preserved when a guard fails).

title: fix(tmp): task scratch dirs need owner-bound lifetime; 7-day age sweep let one task fill 103 GB
body:
## What

Give per-task/per-run scratch directories under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` a bounded lifetime, so a directory created for a task is removed when its owner finishes (or after a short maximum age), instead of waiting for the 7-day age sweep. Make it usable by any project's tooling, not only headless workers.

## Why

Observed on a shared Ubuntu host (2026-11-07): one interactive session created a task base directory in the framework tmp root (used as a short `TMPDIR` for a project's local-verification harness). Each harness run created a fresh `mkdtemp` child with a source export, a 4.7 GiB installed dependency tree and a build, and never removed it. 29 runs in ~36 hours produced **103 GB**; `/home` reached 94% used. `system-cleanup.sh` behaved as designed and did not touch it: entries are pruned only when the top-level entry is older than `AIDEVOPS_TMP_RETENTION_DAYS` (7) **and** no descendant changed within 7 days. Manual deletion was required (the agent cannot `rm -rf` under home by policy).

Existing pieces cover only part of this:
- `system-cleanup.sh` (GH#32485): age-only, 7 days, top-level, moves to trash.
- `sensitive-temp-helper.sh` (GH#35083): owner-exit + max-lifetime guardians, but only for `~/.aidevops-private/tmp` and used by headless runtime only.
- `storage-cleanup-helper.sh` / r922: on-demand and routine entry points; no disk-pressure trigger.

Hazard found while investigating: `system-cleanup.sh:114` skips any directory containing a `*.lock` or `*.lease` file **at any age**, so a stale lease/lock left by a killed producer keeps a directory forever.

## Reproducer

Setup: `mkdir -p "$AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR/task-x/run-1"`, write a large file into `run-1`, repeat `run-2..N` over a day.

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh --dry-run`

**Actual output:** no `[dry-run] Would trash: .../task-x` line until 7 days after the last write inside it; after `touch -d '30 days ago'` on every entry plus `touch .../task-x/run-1/x.lease`, still no line, at any age.

**Expected:** `task-x` becomes eligible as soon as its owner has exited or its max age has passed; a dead owner's lease does not protect it.

## How

- Add a task-scoped temp API, preferably by extending `sensitive-temp-helper.sh` (reuse its owner-exit/max-age guardian) or a thin `task-temp-helper.sh` built on it: `create <task> [--max-age <dur>]` prints a private 0700 dir under the tmp root and records a small owner manifest (owner PID + start time, session/task id, created, expires).
- `system-cleanup.sh`: an entry with a manifest is eligible when its owner is gone (PID+start-time mismatch) or `expires` passed, regardless of the 7-day window; `*.lock`/`*.lease` only protect while their owner is alive (or younger than the retention window), not forever.
- Disk pressure: when free space on the tmp filesystem is below a threshold (e.g. 10% or `AIDEVOPS_TMP_MIN_FREE_GB`), prune expired/ownerless entries first, largest first; never live-owned ones. Log one summary line.
- On Linux, trash on the same filesystem does not free space; under pressure delete instead of trashing (keep trash on macOS/default).
- Guidance: short pointer in `reference/` (not always-loaded AGENTS.md) that task bases / large harness output must use the helper; the harness may keep only small receipts (e.g. `report.json`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sensitive-temp-helper.sh`

title: Worker-origin issues stranded at status:available without auto-dispatch after draft-checkpoint, sweep or stale-recovery paths
body:
## Observed

In one managed project repo, three open worker-origin issues sat at `status:available` with no `auto-dispatch`, no `no-auto-dispatch` and no open PR, for 1, 6 and 17 days. Pulse never dispatches them, and nothing surfaces them as held. A maintainer review on 2026-11-07 restored `auto-dispatch` by hand. Each one reached the stranded state by a different path:

1. **Draft-checkpoint release after the PR had already merged.** A partial PR merged as a ready (non-draft) PR with a non-closing `For #N` reference. About 35 minutes later, the worker released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_draft_checkpoint` and removed `auto-dispatch` ("Draft checkpoint: partial work is preserved on the draft PR. Pulse continues the exact head"). No draft PR existed for the issue: every task PR was merged or closed. So exact-head continuation had nothing to continue. The merged-partial-continuation heal (`pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`), which had restored `auto-dispatch` after the three earlier partial merges on the same issue, did not fire for this merge.
2. **Stale-lifecycle sweep restores status without the dispatch label.** A daily-sweep worker comment ("Stale lifecycle recovery") returned an issue to `status:available` and cleared the stale assignee, "so the next deterministic dispatch pass can pick it up". `auto-dispatch` had been removed at an earlier `worker_ready_missing_linkage` release and was not restored, so no dispatch pass could pick it up.
3. **t2008 stale-recovery escalation, then a status change outside the release helper.** After a t2008 escalation (`status:blocked`, `auto-dispatch` removed), the issue later returned to `status:available` without the `stale-recovery-release:verified` path. `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh release-stale-recovery` then refuses it, because it requires `status:blocked` (`_ddh_release_stale_recovery`, label predicate). So the documented maintainer release no longer applies, and the issue stays undispatchable.

## Relevant code

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_project_post_release_state`: the `worker_draft_checkpoint` branch projects `available` and relies on draft exact-head continuation. It does not verify that an open draft PR still exists for the issue.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_finalize_exit_trap`: `_recover_dirty_worker_pr` / `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` classify the release as `worker_draft_checkpoint`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`: the heal that restores `status:available` plus `auto-dispatch` after a merged non-closing partial.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` `_ddh_release_stale_recovery`: requires `status:blocked`.

## Suggested fix (worker to verify)

- At draft-checkpoint release, check for an open draft PR linked to the issue. If none exists and a non-closing partial PR has merged, project as `worker_merged_partial` (or run the merged-partial heal) so `auto-dispatch` is restored.
- Add a deterministic pulse invariant: an open, unassigned worker-origin issue at `status:available` with no `auto-dispatch`/`no-auto-dispatch`/`parent-task`/`hold-for-review`, no open PR and no live lease is either re-labelled `auto-dispatch` (with an audit comment) or surfaced in the pulse health summary. Respect cost-breaker, recovery-loop and t2008 escalation markers.
- Let `release-stale-recovery` accept `status:available` when the latest escalation marker has no matching release marker.

## Verification

Extend the existing tests (`tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, `tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`) to cover: draft-checkpoint release with no open draft but a merged partial; a sweep-restored available issue with no dispatch label; and stale-recovery release from `status:available`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`

title: fix(pulse): main dispatch still skipped every other cycle; pre-dispatch stages overrun the GH#33560 dispatch reserve
body:
## Observed

On one macOS runner (v3.39.131, about 68 pulse repos, `max_workers=20`), main dispatch still skips about every other cycle, and refill passes skip in the cycles that do dispatch. #36603 / PR #36615 did not remove this. The supervisor sweep at 2026-11-07T09:45Z found **1 active worker of 20**, with 11 `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` candidates in one product repo.

Counts below come from the retained `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (no timestamps on these lines):

- 144 occurrences of `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (... floor=600s prestage_margin=60s enumeration=300–483s)` (GH#33560 gate). In the most recent window, remaining was negative (−11 s to −126 s, once −2820 s) on the skipped main passes. The main pass ran 11 times and was skipped 17 times.
- Every cycle that dispatches then logs `Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget (remaining=62–589s, required=1050–1233s)` and `Event refill drain (cycle-final) skipped ... remaining=-8s..-33s`. Refills therefore never run.
- Passes that do run launch 0–4 workers: `PRIORITY_RESERVATION requested=7–11 product_launched=0–4 held=4–10 discovery_complete=false`. Because discovery never completes inside the budget, the reservation holds most requested slots every pass.
- Stage timeouts eating the pre-dispatch budget (whole retained log): `fix_the_fixer_detector` 60 s ×40, `build_dependency_graph_cache` 600 s ×26, `cleanup_stale_temp_worktrees` 60 s ×24, `reconcile_new_external_issues` 60 s ×14, `cache_prime` 300 s ×13, `auto_decomposer_scanner` 600 s ×6, `normalize_active_issue_assignments` 184–219 s ×13+, `stale_queued_runs` 79–186 s ×10.
- `pulse-check-helper.sh json` at the same time: queue scan `queue_budget_exhausted`, 43 gh errors, `fleet_activity_state=unknown`. In the last hour there were 7 worker events (5 success), all on one provider, with 2 accounts idle.

## Expected

When slots are free and admissible candidates exist, at least one main dispatch pass per cycle runs with its enumeration and per-candidate budget reserved. Housekeeping that overruns is what gets deferred, not dispatch.

## Likely cause

The GH#33560 / GH#36603 gates compare the *remaining* budget with the dispatch reserve after optional stages have run. Stages that hit their own timeouts (dependency graph 600 s, cache prime 300 s, auto-decomposer 600 s) can use up the cycle before the check. #36951, which is open, addresses dependency-graph checkpointing and reconciliation clamping, but not the ordering or reservation itself.

## How

- Reserve the dispatch budget (enumeration + floor + prestage margin) *before* running optional pre-dispatch stages. When a stage would cut into the reservation, defer it (`Stage deferred: ... cycle budget exhausted` already exists for later stages).
- Files to inspect (repo paths): `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:833` (reserve gate message), `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:601` (post-label skip), `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:1351` (priority reservation with `discovery_complete=false`), and the stage sequencing and timeouts in `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh` and the dispatch engine (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`). Which function orders the pre-dispatch stages is not yet confirmed; locate it first.
- Coordinate with open PR #36951 and do not duplicate its dependency-graph and reconciliation changes.
- Keep every existing ownership, API admission, dedup and per-repo cap gate unchanged.

## Verification

- Reproducer: on a runner with many repos, `rg -c "skipped before candidate enumeration" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, compared with `rg -c "Dispatch path=max complete"` over the same window. Before the fix, skips outnumber completed passes.
- After deploying, over 6+ cycles: completed main passes ≥ cycles, skipped main passes ≈ 0 while `active_workers < target`, and `PRIORITY_RESERVATION ... launched` rises when admissible candidates exist.
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh` pass.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`

Reservation is owned by main() and enforced at the shared watchdog stage boundary until main dispatch; dispatch invocations retain their existing admission budgets. PR #36951 checkpointing and reconciliation remain out of scope.

title: fix(pulse): signed-approved external issues without Files Scope blocked forever as brief_scope_untrusted_author
body:
## Observed

An external-contributor `auto-dispatch` issue that already has a verified signed maintainer approval (`sudo aidevops approve issue N`) never dispatches. The issue body has no canonical Files Scope, because the external reporter wrote it and the maintainer triage review comment holds the brief. Editing the body would also change the approval's body content digest.

Evidence from one runner's `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (v3.39.131), for one public-plugin repo issue labelled `external-contributor, auto-dispatch, tier:standard, status:available`, signed approval comment present:

- 14 occurrences of `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=missing_worker_context signal=brief_scope_untrusted_author`. That is one per dispatch pass that reached it, each costing about 21 s of the dispatch budget (`elapsed_ms=21115`).
- Its triage review states "maintainer approval lets the pulse dispatch a worker", which the code path contradicts.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1032-1036` (`_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict`): when `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` returns 40 (no canonical scope), `_brief_scope_author_trusted` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh:60-70`) accepts only write-capable collaborators. A verified signed maintainer approval is not considered, so the GH#33243 worker-owned scope discovery is unreachable for approved external issues. The candidate also stays `status:available`, so it is retried on every pass.

## How

- In the `untrusted_author` branch, treat the issue as trusted for worker-owned scope discovery only when the existing signed-approval verifier (the one `auto_approve_maintainer_issues` / the t1894 path uses) confirms a valid approval bound to the **current** body/title digests. Mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Unsigned, stale-digest or forged approvals must still return 1.
- Do not rewrite the external body (that would invalidate the digest). The worker records the scope as its first step, per the GH#33243 contract.
- Until the issue becomes dispatchable, stop re-attempting the same unchanged untrusted body on every pass: reuse the body-hash marker / footprint-defer pattern so the budget is not spent each cycle.
- Reference pattern: `_brief_scope_worker_discovery_enabled` and the existing signed-approval verification in the NMR auto-approval path. The verifier's exact function is not yet confirmed; locate it with `rg -n "aidevops-signed-approval" .agents/scripts`.

## Verification

- A focused regression next to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` / `test-pulse-dispatch-missing-context.sh`, with three cases. External author + valid signed approval + no Files Scope gives verdict 0 (dispatch with worker discovery). External author without approval gives `untrusted_author`, rc=1. Approval whose body digest no longer matches gives rc=1.
- After deploy, the observed issue logs `dispatching with worker-owned scope discovery (GH#33243)` instead of `brief_scope_untrusted_author`.
- ShellCheck clean on changed scripts.

title: circuit-breaker: sibling investigation issue created with empty body (footer only) since ~v3.39.131
body:
## What

Since about v3.39.131, `circuit-breaker-helper.sh::_cb_file_investigation_task` can create
its sibling "Investigate circuit-breaker trip" issue with an empty body: the
issue contains only the origin/signature markers and footer. The labels are
applied correctly (`bug`, `auto-dispatch`, `tier:thinking`, `framework`,
`source:circuit-breaker-investigation`), so the empty issue still dispatches
at `tier:thinking`, but the worker gets no brief, no trip reference and no
resolution options.

## Observed evidence (2026-11-07)

- A runner on v3.39.131 tripped its breaker at 09:58:08Z with 3 consecutive
  `worker_spawn_failed` failures. The last task was #37046 in this repo.
- The trip notification issue was created in a managed private project repo
  with its full body and the `circuit-breaker` and `source:circuit-breaker`
  labels.
- The sibling investigation issue, titled `Investigate circuit-breaker trip
  #<trip>: worker_spawn_failed after 3 consecutive failures`, was created 28 s
  later in the same repo. Its body is 119 characters:
  `<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->`, `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`, `---` and the
  v3.39.131 automated-scan footer. All of the
  `_cb_build_investigation_body` content (What/Why/How, around 4 KB) is missing.
- Known-good reference: #36390 (2026-11-01, v3.39.108) was created by the same
  path with a 3,977-character body.
- Current `main` `circuit-breaker-helper.sh` (lines 744-798) still builds the
  body, appends `gh-signature-helper.sh footer --body "$body"`, and passes
  `--body "$body"` to `gh_create_issue`. The loss therefore probably happens
  downstream in `gh_create_issue`/signature/origin-marker composition, or in the
  body builder's command substitution. This is unverified: the failing
  runner's logs are not available from the reporting host.

## Secondary observation

The trip and its investigation were both filed in the project repo that the
pulse was running in (`_cb_resolve_repo_slug` uses `gh repo view` in the
current directory). The failing task, however, was a framework-repo issue,
and the cause (`worker_spawn_failed`) can only be diagnosed from the tripping
runner's own logs. A worker that another runner dispatches on the
investigation issue cannot reach that evidence. Consider recording the
tripping runner/device in the body and routing investigation to the failing
task's repo, or to the framework repo for framework tasks.

## How

- Files: `.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-helper.sh`
  (`_cb_build_investigation_body` ~667-728, `_cb_file_investigation_task`
  ~744-798); `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` (`gh_create_issue` and
  any body rewrite or origin-marker injection); and
  `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` if footer handling changed after
  v3.39.108.
- Reproduce: source the helper under a test harness that stubs `gh`, call
  `_cb_file_investigation_task owner/repo 1 3 owner/repo#2 worker_spawn_failed`,
  and assert that the `--body` argument received by the stub contains `## What`
  and `Ref #1`.
- Fix the dropping layer. If the body cannot be composed, fail closed rather
  than creating an empty `auto-dispatch` issue.

## Acceptance

- The investigation issue body contains the full `_cb_build_investigation_body`
  text plus a single footer.
- An empty or failed body composition does not create an auto-dispatch issue.
- A regression test covers the body reaching `gh_create_issue`.

title: permission broker: add ~/.local/bin to read-only toolchain roots (workers stall on sudo approval for tool discovery)
body:
## What

Headless workers stop at a `sudo`-gated maintainer permission request when
they read `~/.local/bin/*`. The permission broker auto-allows read-only
toolchain roots, but its list has a single entry:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-read-only-root.mjs:6`:
  `const READ_ONLY_ROOTS = ["~/.nvm"];`

The framework itself already treats `~/.local/bin` as a standard binary
location:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:1752` lists
  `"${HOME}/.local/bin/${binary_name}"` as a candidate, and line 1763 lists
  `fixed_candidate_dirs="/opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin, ~/.opencode/bin"`.

## Observed evidence (2026-11-06, Linux runner, v3.39.128)

Two separate award-enrichment issues in a managed private project repo were
released as `permission_required`, labelled `needs-maintainer-permissions`, and
then sat for more than 24 hours. Each needed this command:
`sudo aidevops approve permissions issue <N> <repo> --request <id>` (or
`--withdraw`).

- Requests `perm-33deb3b42f417a64` (04:01Z) and `perm-730587499ce5b8f8`
  (19:33Z).
- Both asked for `external_directory` via `read` on `~/.local/bin/*`, risk
  `medium`, `grantable: true`.
- The broker's own recovery text for both says that routine tool discovery
  should use `command -v TOOL`, `TOOL --version` or a repository wrapper. The
  capability was never needed, yet each stall still costs a human `sudo` step
  and leaves an award blocked.

## How

Pick one or both:

1. Add `~/.local/bin` (and possibly the other read-only binary roots that
   `headless-runtime-lib.sh` already probes, such as `~/.opencode/bin`) to
   `READ_ONLY_ROOTS`. Existing guards are unchanged: writes stay rejected,
   `FORBIDDEN_PATTERN` credential paths stay rejected, and `..` escapes stay
   rejected.
2. For read-only `external_directory` requests that the recovery text classes
   as tool discovery, reject them in-session with that recovery hint and let
   the worker continue. Do not release the claim and raise a maintainer
   permission request for them.

Reference pattern: the existing `~/.nvm` test in
`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs:156-194`
("headless workers auto-allow read-only toolchain roots but never writes or
credential files"). Extend it with `~/.local/bin/*` read (allowed), write
(rejected) and escape (rejected) cases.

## Acceptance

- A headless read of `~/.local/bin/*` no longer creates a maintainer
  permission request or releases the claim.
- Writes under `~/.local/bin` and `..` escapes are still rejected.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
  passes.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.131 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.5 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 5d 9h and 14,299,496 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-read-only-root.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`

Implementation: add only `~/.local/bin` to the existing read-only roots; preserve all existing write, forbidden-path, and traversal guards. Extend the existing broker test to cover allowed reads without handoff and rejected writes, credential paths, and non-credential traversal. Verification: `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`.

title: Buzz runtime reinstall: refresh imported agents' source digests in place
body:
## Problem

Every aidevops update that changes an agent's instruction file breaks the Buzz agents imported from the team snapshot, once the interactive runtime anchor is reinstalled.

Each imported Buzz agent stores a pointer prompt with `Expected source digest: sha256:<digest>` for its `agents:<file>.md` source. At launch, `_team_interface_buzz_runtime_prepare.py` (`prepare_runtime`) compares Buzz's `BUZZ_ACP_SYSTEM_PROMPT` with `member_system_prompt()` built from the anchor and fails closed on any difference. Once the anchor is reinstalled with newer instruction files, every agent fails to start. Re-importing the team does not help because Buzz import is create-only: it mints new identities and strands existing DMs and threads (`.agents/reference/team-interface-buzz-provisioning.md`, "Safety and lifecycle").

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** after `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --runtime interactive --replace` (2026-11-07, first successful reinstall after #37001), send a DM to `aidevops-marcus-macbook-pro-01` in Buzz Desktop 0.5.28.

**Actual output** (Buzz agent log):

```
team-interface-buzz-runtime: Buzz agent source pointer or digest does not match the canonical roster
ERROR buzz_acp: agent initialize failed: Agent process exited unexpectedly agent=0
```

The message shows only a 👀 reaction and no reply. Of 30 aidevops records (15 per community), 22 held August digests; for example `aidevops.md` `fb441254…` saved versus `5265bf1d…` in the anchor.

The maintainer-approved manual repair: with Buzz quit, back up `managed-agents.json`, then rewrite only the `Expected source digest:` line of records whose prompt starts with `Aidevops canonical source:` and whose name matches a current snapshot member. Skip any record whose other lines differ. The agents started again with identities intact.

## Expected

Reinstalling the interactive runtime (Buzz must already be stopped) also refreshes the stored digests in place:

- Before replacing the manifest, back up Buzz's `agents/managed-agents.json` to `~/.aidevops/buzz-backups/` (mode 600), the same as the manifest rollback copy.
- For each record whose `system_prompt` is an aidevops pointer prompt and whose `name` maps to a current roster member for this host, change only the digest line. Leave any record with other differing lines unchanged and report it.
- Print a per-agent summary (name, old and new 12-character digest prefix) and never print other store fields.
- Keep the launch check strict. This makes the owner-run reinstall the explicit point where new instructions are accepted, instead of weakening the check.
- Update `.agents/reference/team-interface-buzz-provisioning.md` to say that a reinstall refreshes digests in place, and to give the rollback path.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-runtime.py`

- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py`
- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_snapshot_member.py`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_digest_refresh.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/team-interface-buzz-provisioning.md`

Reference pattern: the manifest backup in the install flow (`~/.aidevops/buzz-backups/aidevops-interactive-v1.<ts>.json`) and the running-app guard `buzz_is_running()` in `_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py`. Build the expected prompt with `member_system_prompt()` and `buzz_display_name()` from the new anchor's agents tree, not the mutable deployment.

Integration scope recovery: `install_manifest()` in `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py` owns the stopped-app guard, manifest collision check and early idempotent return. This caller must invoke digest refresh using the new pinned agents tree before manifest replacement, including unchanged-manifest reinstalls. No competing PR targets this caller; the assigned worker retains ownership. Verification remains the two runtime suites below.

## Verification

- Extend `test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs`: a fixture store with one stale-digest pointer record, one record whose prompt differs on another line, and one non-aidevops record. After install, only the first changes, a backup exists, and running the install again changes nothing.
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-runtime.mjs` and `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-installed-startup.mjs` pass.

title: Buzz remote-interactive anchor broken by greeting background redeploy
body:
## What happened

A Buzz remote-interactive agent (`aidevops-full-interactive-v1` harness) started once on a fresh runtime anchor, then every later start failed:

```
team-interface-buzz-runtime: pinned OpenCode config does not select the anchored plugin
[ERROR] Remote interactive runtime anchor content verification failed
buzz_acp: agent initialize failed: Agent process exited unexpectedly
```

## Root cause

1. `opencode-launcher-helper.sh` `run_remote_interactive_session` exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<anchor>/opencode-config` for the agent's OpenCode process.
2. The plugin greeting runs `aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive`. `_check_script_drift` (and `_hotfix_auto_apply`) then start `setup.sh` in the background. GH#33046 unsets `OPENCODE_CONFIG`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, but `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is still inherited.
3. `setup/_opencode_config_paths.sh` `_opencode_config_user_roots` treats `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/opencode` as user-owned. `setup_opencode_plugins` rewrote the anchor's `opencode.json` plugin entry to `file://~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` and added a `plugins/` symlink to the live deploy.
4. `_team_interface_buzz_runtime_anchor.py:234-236` rejects the anchor on the next start.

Evidence: the anchor's `opencode.json` and `tui.json` have mtime 12:22:46, which matches `setup_opencode_plugins` at 12:22:46 in `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`. The agent's OpenCode session started at 12:21:52.

## Fix

`.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`: add `_in_isolated_runtime_session` (true when `AIDEVOPS_REMOTE_RUNTIME_ANCHOR`, `AIDEVOPS_REMOTE_INTERFACE=1` or `AIDEVOPS_TEAM_INTERFACE_OVERLAY` is set). Skip the script-drift redeploy and the hotfix auto-apply in those sessions. The host auto-update daemon redeploys from a clean environment.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` passes.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-update-check-gh-slurp-prerequisite.sh` passes 6/6.
- Runtime: reinstall the interactive anchor (`team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --runtime interactive --replace`), start the Buzz agent, send a message, then confirm the anchor's `opencode.json` mtime is unchanged and the next agent start passes verification.

Out of scope: an already-broken anchor needs a reinstall.

title: document forensics: detect vertical flips, tolerate fractional page-size drift, avoid false rotations
body:
## What

`document-creation-helper.sh forensics` (from #28702) could not repair a real corpus of scanned planning drawings. Three defects found while auditing 36 image-only PDFs (73 pages):

1. **Vertical flips are never tested.** Two A1 drawings were scanned upside-down-mirrored, i.e. flipped about the horizontal axis: glyphs upside down but reading left to right, title block top-right, building elevations inverted. The candidate set is `original`, `flip-horizontal`, `rotate-90/180/270`. A vertical flip equals `rotate-180` + `flip-horizontal` and is not reachable from any single candidate, so these pages can only end up `normal` or `uncertain`.
2. **Exact string comparison of fractional page dimensions** marks every affected file `partial` and suppresses the readable PDF. Source `2327x1642` vs rendered derivative `2327.04x1642.08` (300 dpi round-trip) fails at `document-forensics-lib.sh` `_df_annotate_page_dimensions` (`[[ "$derived_dimensions" != "$source_dimensions" ]]`) and `_df_verify_readable_pdf` (same comparison). Result: `readable_pdf: null` even for pages classified `normal`.
3. **False positive rotation.** A plainly upright, high-quality A4 application form page (original OCR confidence 87.8, 261 words) was classified `rotated` / `rotate-90` with improvement 23 (threshold 15). Publishing this would have rotated a correct page.

Also observed: about 1 minute per page on A1 drawings (approx. 9,700 px wide at 300 dpi × 5 OCR candidates), which makes whole-application audits impractical without parallelism.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/document-forensics-lib.sh`: candidate generation (the `-flop` / `-rotate` block around the `magick ... -flop` call): add `flip-vertical` (`magick -flip`) and map it to a `mirrored` classification with an explicit `selected_transform`.
- `.agents/scripts/document-forensics-lib.sh` `_df_annotate_page_dimensions` and `_df_verify_readable_pdf`: compare numerically with a tolerance (for example ≤ 0.5 pt, or ≤ 1 px at render dpi) instead of string equality.
- `.agents/scripts/document-forensics-lib.sh` suspect-page selection (`best_transform` / `_DF_MIN_IMPROVEMENT` block): require a relative gain as well as an absolute one when the original already has sufficient evidence (high confidence + word count), so a strong upright original cannot be overridden by a marginal rotation score.
- Consider a lossless repair path for readable output: apply a page `/Rotate` or a content-stream `cm` transform (e.g. `[1 0 0 -1 0 H]` for a vertical flip) instead of re-rasterising, which also removes the dimension drift.
- `.agents/tools/document/document-creation.md` "PDF Forensics": document the candidate set, including `flip-vertical`.

## Reference pattern

The working manual repair was a pypdf content transform on the cloned page: `Transformation().scale(1, -1).translate(0, y0 + y1)` for a vertical flip, `scale(-1, 1).translate(x0 + x1, 0)` for a horizontal flip. Output size stayed within 0.003% of the source, with no image re-encode.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/document-forensics-lib.sh .agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-document-forensics-helper.sh
```

Add fixtures: (a) a vertically flipped text page must classify `mirrored` with `selected_transform: flip-vertical`; (b) a source page with non-integer-at-300dpi dimensions must not record a dimension failure and must publish `readable_pdf`; (c) an upright high-confidence page must remain `normal`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Vertically flipped scans are detected and repaired.
- Sub-point dimension drift does not mark runs `partial` or suppress readable output.
- Upright high-confidence pages are never re-oriented.
