title: worker-lifecycle: skip Linux-only /proc live-process test on non-Linux hosts
body:
## Problem

`ReconstructibleContract.test_real_live_process_cwd_and_fd_are_observed` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py` (~L207) reads `/proc/<pid>` for a real child process. On macOS `/proc` does not exist. The census raises `proc-observation-unavailable` and the test fails instead of skipping.

The CI step "Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract" (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, ~L684) only runs on Linux, so CI never sees this. Locally on macOS the full lifecycle suite always reports 1 failure, which hides real regressions.

## Reproducer

On macOS (observed with Python 3.15), from the repo root on current `main`:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest -v tests.test_reconstructible.ReconstructibleContract.test_real_live_process_cwd_and_fd_are_observed
```

Result:

```
AssertionError: "live-process-reference" does not match "proc-observation-unavailable"
FAILED (failures=1)
```

The full suite (`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests` with the same `PYTHONPATH`) reports 344 tests, 1 failure, 3 skipped. The same failure occurs on a worktree based on `main` before #37084, so it predates #37084.

## Fix

Add the existing platform guard pattern from `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py:215`:

```python
@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "linux", "Linux /proc process observation")
```

on `test_real_live_process_cwd_and_fd_are_observed`. Import `sys` if the module does not already import it. Do not change the Linux contract or the census code.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py`

## Verification

- macOS: the reproducer command above reports the test as `skipped`, with no failures.
- Linux CI: the "Verify Worker Lifecycle Linux contract" step still runs and passes this test.
- `ruff check --no-cache .agents/worker-lifecycle` clean.

title: wp-dev.md: warn that get_posts(name=>slug) never matches pages in slug-exists guards
body:
## Observed

While writing a WP-CLI `eval-file` script to clone a page, I added an idempotency guard that checks the target slug does not already exist:

```php
$existing = get_posts( array( 'name' => $slug, 'numberposts' => 1 ) );
```

The guard can never fire for pages. `get_posts()` defaults to `post_type => 'post'` and `post_status => 'publish'`, so it never matches an existing page with that slug, published or draft. This only surfaced because a separate check in the same script queried `wp_posts.post_name` directly and disagreed with the guard.

The current WordPress guidance does not warn about this, so an agent writing a clone or create script can ship a silent no-op guard and create duplicate pages (WordPress then assigns `slug-2`).

## Proposed change

- **File:** `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md`, section "WP-CLI Quick Reference".
- **Change:** add one short line on slug-exists checks before creating a page or CPT. Pass `post_type` and `post_status => 'any'` explicitly, or use `get_page_by_path( $slug, OBJECT, 'page' )`, or query `$wpdb->posts` by `post_name` and `post_type`. Note that `'any'` excludes trashed posts, and a trashed post keeps its slug with a `__trashed` suffix.
- **Reference pattern:** the existing one-line gotcha style of the "Page cache on shared LiteSpeed hosting" paragraph in the same file.

## Verification

- `rg -n "get_page_by_path|post_status" .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md` shows the new line.
- Run the repo's markdown lint on the changed file.
- Optional check on any WP install: `wp eval 'var_dump( count( get_posts( array( "name" => "<existing-page-slug>" ) ) ) );'` returns `0`, and the same call with `"post_type" => "page", "post_status" => "any"` returns `1`.

title: t2449 worker-briefed gate reports no linked issue despite Resolves #N closing reference
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo> --squash` keeps failing with `Merge blocked by t2449: no linked issue (t2449)` for an `origin:worker` PR. GitHub reports a closing reference: `gh pr view <PR> --json closingIssuesReferences` returns `[<issue>]`, and the PR body contains a plain `Resolves #<issue>` line.

- Before the body edit: the body had `For #<issue>` and the title had a `GH#<issue>:` prefix. The deterministic merge pass logged `no linked issue (t2449)` on four cycles (pulse.log).
- After the supervisor changed `For` to `Resolves`, the gate still failed on three attempts across about 5 minutes. That is longer than the snapshot cache TTLs (`AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_TTL` 15s, `AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FALLBACK_CACHE_TTL` 20s).
- The PR is otherwise mergeable: CI green, author has admin permission, review-bot gate `PASS_RATE_LIMITED`, data-only files.

## Why it matters

Before the edit, `_extract_pr_work_issue <pr> <repo> explicit` returned empty for a `For #N` body plus a `GH#N:` title. A worker PR that follows the narrow-scope convention therefore never reaches `_worker_briefed_trust_check` with a linked issue. After the edit, the closing keyword path in `_extract_linked_issue` → `_gh_pr_body_closing_issues` should match `Resolves #N` but apparently does not in the full-loop subshell. The cause is unverified. Candidates: the body read inside `_merge_worker_briefed_trust_gate` (sources `pulse-merge.sh` in a subshell) returns a different body, or the explicit-mode parse rejects the body.

title: Buzz 0.5.28 agent replies not published: ACP proxy ignores tagged prompt sections
body:
## What happened

In Buzz Desktop 0.5.28 the `aidevops-full-interactive-v1` agent produces a reply, and the Buzz activity panel shows `<buzz-reply>Hi! What would you like to work on?</buzz-reply>`. The reply is never posted to the DM. The agent log has no error: the turn ends normally.

## Reproducer

1. Buzz Desktop 0.5.28 with an aidevops remote-interactive agent started on a current runtime anchor.
2. DM the agent `hello`.
3. Observed: the activity panel shows the `<buzz-reply>` text and token usage, but no message appears in the DM.
4. Replay the stored session prompt through `trustedReplyDestination`: it returns `null`.

## Root cause

Buzz 0.5.28 sends prompt sections as tagged blocks:

```
<context>
Scope: dm
Channel: DM (#<uuid>)
...
</context>

<buzz-event type="@mention">
Event ID: <64-hex>
Channel: DM (#<uuid>)
...
Content: hello
Tags: [...]
</buzz-event>
```

`.agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs` recognises only the older bracket headers (`[Context]`, `[Buzz event: …]`). `trustedReplyDestination` returns `null`, `TurnState.begin` records no turn, and `team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs` never calls `publishReply`.

## Fix

In `_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs`, map a `<context>` or `<buzz-event type="…">` section to the bracket form only when it spans the whole prompt block. The existing trust checks then run unchanged on both formats. `isDirectGreeting` uses the same normalised blocks.

## Verification

- Replaying the real failing session prompt: before `null`; after `{"channel":"69425898-…","directGreeting":true,"replyTo":"245bd997…"}`.
- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs`: pass.
- `bunx biome check .agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs`: clean.
- Runtime: after deploy and runtime reinstall, DM the agent and confirm the reply appears in the DM.

Not handled, same as before: batched `<buzz-events>` turns.

title: fix(lifecycle): admission cleanup starves on dead parent-missing rows and never-closed admissions (~1 retire/pass)
body:
## Problem

Automatic admission cleanup (`cleanup_pass` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py`) retires about one worktree per pass on the shared Linux Pulse host, while workers create 40–80 a day per runner. Disk drops about 47 GB a day and has needed manual guarded reclaims six times. Two causes are separate from #37034, which covers the observation-era takeover reporting:

1. **Dead admission rows starve the rotation.** `generation_admissions` keeps rows for temporary paths whose parent directory no longer exists. These are test fixtures run inside worker worktrees (`…/.agent-workspace/tmp/test-remote-branch-cleanup.*/…`, `…/tmp/buzz-installed-startup-*/…`) and archive restore scratch dirs (`…/recovery/archives/.producer-transactions/*/.restore-*`). `reconcile_absence()` (`absence.py:92`) returns `source-absence-unconfirmed` / `parent-missing` for them on every pass, counted as `held`. They are never removed, and each still takes one of the pass's 25 slots (`limit=25`).
2. **Finished worktrees keep an `open` admission.** Clean worktrees whose PR merged and whose head is pushed still have `generation_admissions.state='open'` hours after the worker exited. The observation-era takeover then fails with `managed-admission-not-closed` (`legacy_takeover._require_closed_admission`). So the #37034 fix will report the real reason but still cannot retire them.

## Evidence (read-only, 2026-11-07 ~18:30 UTC, v3.39.132)

Registry census of `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worker-lifecycle/registry.sqlite3`:

| runner | rows | temp/restore, parent missing | real worktree, exists, open | real worktree, exists, closed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 617 | **419 (68%)** | 176 | 2 |
| B | 247 | 46 | 153 | 29 |

- Log: runner A's `cleanup_worktrees.log` shows 1,413 `source-absence-unconfirmed`/`parent-missing` results in its last 4,000 lines.
- Retired per pass: `Lifecycle cleanup:` summaries over the last 40 passes show `retired=49` (A) and `retired=25` (B). Passes run about every 1–2 h.
- Stuck worktrees: of 96 worktrees that are clean, pushed, merged-PR and idle ≥6 h, 73 have `state='open'` admissions and never appear in cleanup results. Runner B also has 22 `closed` ones that hit repeated `verify-local` archive failures, which #36801 now quarantines.
- Disk impact: shared `/home` went from 84% to 89% (159 GB to 112 GB free) in 24 h after the last manual reclaim. The dispatch floor is 5%.

## Reproducer

On a Pulse host with the lifecycle registry, run this as the runner user:

```python
import os, sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
db = Path.home() / ".aidevops/.agent-workspace/worker-lifecycle/registry.sqlite3"
c = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
rows = c.execute("SELECT path, state FROM generation_admissions").fetchall()
dead = [p for p, _ in rows if not os.path.isdir(os.path.dirname(p))]
print(len(rows), "rows;", len(dead), "with missing parent")
```

A large missing-parent count reproduces cause 1.

**Symptom command:** `grep -a 'Lifecycle cleanup:' ~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log | tail -n 4`

**Actual output** (runner A):

```
[pulse-wrapper] Lifecycle cleanup: retired=2 failed=0 held=16 archive_failed=0 reconciled=2 quarantined=0
[pulse-wrapper] Lifecycle cleanup: retired=1 failed=0 held=5 archive_failed=0 reconciled=0 quarantined=0
[pulse-wrapper] Lifecycle cleanup: retired=0 failed=0 held=25 archive_failed=0 reconciled=0 quarantined=0
```

**Expected:** most passes retire several eligible trees, and `held` does not include rows whose source parent no longer exists.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/absence.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/admission.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_absence.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_admission.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-remote-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-installed-startup.mjs`

Integration evidence: registry zipapp import failed in test_bundle because cleanup now imports legacy_proc; bundle.py must include that existing module. Verify tests.test_bundle. These named fixtures launch lifecycle-aware Git/worktree operations; worker-lifecycle-state.sh resolves AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DIR before HOME. Isolate each fixture using that override and verify the existing fixture commands.

## Fix (worker-ready)

1. **Parent-missing reconciliation.** When the parent directory is missing *and* the generation has no bound/live run, record a terminal `source-absent-reconciled` event (reason `parent-missing`) and close the admission. Keep the current fail-closed behaviour if any run is still bound or live. This mirrors the existing absent-source path in `absence.py`. Optionally, don't count terminal/absent rows toward `limit`.
2. **Close admission on run end.** Find where a worker run ends (`storage.py` run state → `ended`) and close the generation's admission once every bound run has ended and no launch is pending. Alternatively, let `prepare_retirement` close it under the same condition so the next pass can retire the tree. Do not close it while any run is bound or the worktree has a live process.
3. **Stop leaking test admissions.** Tests that exercise lifecycle code must use a temporary registry (`HOME`/store override), not the runner's real one. Check `.agents/scripts/tests/test-remote-branch-cleanup*.sh` and the `buzz-installed-startup` test.

Do not weaken: dirty/unpushed/open-PR/live-process retention, archive-before-remove, non-forced removal, branch retention, or the disk-capacity floor.

## Verification

- Unit: a registry row whose parent is missing and has no bound run reconciles once and is not re-examined. With a bound run it stays `source-absence-unconfirmed`. Ending the last bound run closes the admission.
- CI: the `Complexity Analysis` worker-lifecycle suite plus ruff/mypy from `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`.
- Runtime: after release, the missing-parent count from the reproducer falls toward 0 within a day. `Lifecycle cleanup:` reports `retired` well above 1 per pass. Worktree counts and `/home` usage stay flat without manual reclaim.

Related: #37034 / PR #37036 (takeover reporting), #36923 (proc observation, merged via #36942), #36798 (quarantine, merged via #36801), #35359.

title: Buzz ACP proxy drops replies for batched and mid-turn (steer) prompts
body:
## What happens

Follow-up to #37096 / PR #37097. Single Buzz events now publish replies. Turns that carry more than one event, or a message that arrives while the agent is still working (the agent runs with `meh=Steer`), still produce no posted reply. The model answers, `trustedReplyDestination` returns `null`, and `team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs` never calls `publishReply`. Nothing is logged.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** save the script below as `check.mjs` in the repo root, then run `node check.mjs`. It feeds a Buzz 0.5.28 `<context>` block plus each event shape into `trustedReplyDestination`.

```js
import {trustedReplyDestination} from "./.agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs";

const ch = "69425898-ab57-4912-b240-a27ead4a2b45";
const id1 = "a".repeat(64);
const id2 = "b".repeat(64);
const context = `<context>\nScope: dm\nChannel: DM (#${ch})\n</context>`;
const event = (id, text) =>
  `Event ID: ${id}\nChannel: DM (#${ch})\nFrom: npub1example\nContent: ${text}\nTags: []\nIMPORTANT: To stay in this thread, use \`--reply-to ${id}\` when sending.`;

const cases = {
  single: `<buzz-event type="@mention">\n${event(id1, "hello")}\n</buzz-event>`,
  batched: `<buzz-events count="2">\n--- Event 1 (@mention) ---\n${event(id1, "one")}\n\n--- Event 2 (@mention) ---\n${event(id2, "two")}\n</buzz-events>`,
  steer: `<new-message-arrived-while-you-were-working>\n--- Event 1 (@mention) ---\n${event(id2, "also this")}\n</new-message-arrived-while-you-were-working>`,
};

for (const [name, eventBlock] of Object.entries(cases)) {
  const message = {params: {prompt: [{type: "text", text: context}, {type: "text", text: eventBlock}]}};
  console.log(name, JSON.stringify(trustedReplyDestination(message)));
}
```

**Actual output:**

```
single {"channel":"69425898-…","directGreeting":true,"replyTo":"aaaa…"}
batched null
steer null
```

**Expected:** `batched` and `steer` resolve to the channel, with `replyTo` taken from the last event (the same anchor Buzz uses; see `format_prompt` in block/buzz `crates/buzz-acp/src/queue.rs`).

Runtime path: DM an aidevops Buzz agent, then send a second message before it replies. The second turn arrives as `<new-message-arrived-while-you-were-working>` and its reply never appears in the DM.

## Event shapes Buzz sends (block/buzz `origin/main`, `format_prompt`)

- `<buzz-events count="N">` with `--- Event i (tag) ---` sub-blocks (several queued events, no cancellation)
- `<new-message-arrived-while-you-were-working[ count="N"]>` (steer), preceded by `<what-you-were-working-on>`
- `<new-request-supersedes-previous[ count="N"]>` (interrupt), preceded by `<previous-request-interrupted-before-completion>`
- Each sub-block uses the same body as a single event: `Event ID`, `Channel`, `From`, `Content`, `Tags`, then an optional `IMPORTANT: … use \`--reply-to <id>\` …` line.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs`: extend `normalizeBlock` / `collectEventBlocks` to accept the multi-event and merge tags. Split on `--- Event i (tag) ---` and treat the **last** new event as the routing event. Never take routing from the cancelled/prior section. Keep every existing trust check: single `<context>`, channel match on every sub-event, one trusted `--reply-to` per event, and rejection of `IMPORTANT` lines inside `Content`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs`: add cases for the three shapes above, plus a negative case where a prior/cancelled section carries a different channel.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs`

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs`
- `bunx biome check .agents/scripts/_team_interface_acp_destination.mjs`
- The reproducer above prints a destination for `batched` and `steer`
- Runtime: after `setup.sh` and a Buzz runtime `--replace` reinstall, send two quick DMs and confirm both turns post replies

## Out of scope

The single-event path (fixed in #37097). Buzz-side prompt format changes.

title: Buzz runtime install --replace leaves unused 171 MB anchors behind
body:
## What happens

Every `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --replace` creates a new immutable anchor under `~/.aidevops/buzz-runtimes/<profile-id>/v2-<agents>-<config>/`. The old anchor is never removed. On one Mac, two framework updates in a day left two unused anchors of 171 MB each next to the live one. Each framework update that changes `agents/` adds another.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `du -sh ~/.aidevops/buzz-runtimes/aidevops-interactive-v1/*` after two `install --runtime interactive --replace` runs separated by a framework `setup.sh` deploy

**Actual output:**

```
171M  …/v2-cccfa7ab9f7737c9-a89cd04ed77b2b6a   (unreferenced)
171M  …/v2-ed835f7e3515d9f4-a89cd04ed77b2b6a   (unreferenced)
171M  …/v2-2d81f812778317d6-a89cd04ed77b2b6a   (referenced by custom_harnesses/aidevops-interactive-v1.json)
```

**Expected:** after a successful install, unreferenced anchors are removed, or `install` reports them and a `prune` subcommand removes them.

## Approach

- In `materialize_pinned_runtime` (`.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_anchor.py:264`) or right after a successful `install` in `.agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-runtime.py`, list sibling `v*-*-*` directories in the same profile parent.
- Keep any anchor referenced by a manifest in Buzz's `custom_harnesses/*.json` (installed app and dev app data dirs), the anchor just installed, and anchors whose agent processes are still running. A `pgrep -f <anchor path>` check is enough.
- Move the rest to the Trash (the repo's trash-backed cleanup pattern), not `rm -rf`. Log each one.
- Add `prune [--dry-run]` as a subcommand so it can also run on its own.

title: docs: bounded operations need aidevops secret NAME -- argv for API keys
body:
## What

`reference/context-efficient-output.md` → "Bounded interactive operations" does not say how a bounded operation gets a secret. In an interactive OpenCode session (aidevops 3.39.127), commands started with `aidevops_bounded_operation` did not see API keys that the session's own shell commands had, so scripts reading `$CRUX_API_KEY` or `$CLOUDFLARE_..._API_TOKEN` ran without them. Agents then retried, or fell back to blocking Bash calls that hit the 300 s shell timeout.

What worked every time: put the secret wrapper in the argv, so the key goes only to the child process and is never printed:

```json
["aidevops", "secret", "CRUX_API_KEY", "--", "bash", "/path/to/psi-batch.sh", "..."]
```

Also not stated there: `output_offset` starts at 1 (0 is rejected).

## Files

- `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`, section "Bounded interactive operations" (about L69–101): add two short sentences:
  1. Bounded operations do not get session secrets. Wrap the command as `aidevops secret NAME -- <argv>`, and never pass a value in argv.
  2. `output_offset` is 1-based.
- Optionally, the `aidevops_bounded_operation` tool description in the OpenCode plugin, if it has room under its size budget.

## Verification

- Start `["aidevops","secret","<any set secret>","--","bash","-c","test -n \"$<NAME>\" && echo set"]` as a bounded operation. The output reads `set`, and the value never appears.
- The reference size ratchet and markdown lint pass.

`.agents/reference/team-interface-buzz-provisioning.md` explains that Buzz agent names come from macOS `LocalHostName` (`aidevops-marcus-macbook-pro-01`). title: Buzz runtime install --replace leaves agents pinned to the old anchor via agent_command_override
body:
## What happens

When a Buzz agent's harness is set to the aidevops interactive runtime, Buzz saves the runtime's absolute command path into that agent's `managed-agents.json` record as `agent_command_override`, e.g. `~/.aidevops/buzz-runtimes/aidevops-interactive-v1/v2-<agents>-<config>/agents/bin/aidevops-buzz-acp-interactive`. `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py install --replace` writes a new anchor and updates `custom_harnesses/aidevops-interactive-v1.json`, but never updates these per-agent overrides.

Effects:

- Those agents keep running the old anchor. They miss every fix since, e.g. #37096 reply routing and #37074 anchor redeploy.
- Removing old anchors (#37118) would break them with no warning.
- `aidevops buzz status` / `reconcile` (`buzz-desktop-helper.sh`) don't report them. Reconcile only recognises the `opencode` / `opencode-acp` wrapper shape.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `python3 -c "import json,pathlib;p=pathlib.Path.home()/'Library/Application Support/xyz.block.buzz.app/agents/managed-agents.json';[print(r.get('name'),r.get('relay_url'),r['agent_command_override'].split('/')[-4]) for r in json.loads(p.read_text()) if 'buzz-runtimes/' in str(r.get('agent_command_override'))]"`

Run it after `install --runtime interactive --replace`. It prints names, relays and anchor names only; never print whole records, which hold auth tags and keys.

**Actual output (2026-11-07, one Mac):**

```
live harness anchor: v2-2d81f812778317d6-a89cd04ed77b2b6a
Fizz   wss://<second relay>  -> v2-99226248dc14145f-00bb29b2b0f650ad
Honey  wss://<second relay>  -> v2-99226248dc14145f-00bb29b2b0f650ad
Pollen wss://<second relay>  -> v2-99226248dc14145f-00bb29b2b0f650ad
```

**Expected:** after install, every override that points at an older anchor of the same runtime id points at the new anchor.

Fixed by hand with Buzz closed: back up the store, rewrite only the overrides matching `<parent>/<anchor>/agents/bin/aidevops-buzz-acp-interactive` for a non-live anchor, keep file mode 600. All three agents then started and went online.

## Approach

- In `install_payload` (`.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py:66`), next to `refresh_source_digests`, repoint stale overrides for the same runtime id to the new anchor command. Only do this when Buzz is stopped (already required) and after the existing store backup. Print counts and agent names only.
- Match strictly: the exact parent `~/.aidevops/buzz-runtimes/<runtime id>/`, an anchor name of `v2-<16hex>-<16hex>` or the legacy `<16hex>-<16hex>`, and the exact `agents/bin/aidevops-buzz-acp-interactive` tail. Leave every other override alone.
- Report stale overrides in `aidevops buzz status` as well, so drift is visible before an install.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/_team_interface_buzz_runtime_install.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/team-interface-buzz-provisioning.md`

## Verification

- Fixture store with one stale, one live and one unrelated override: install repoints only the stale one, and a backup exists in `~/.aidevops/buzz-backups/`
- `aidevops buzz status` reports the stale count before install and 0 after
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh` clean; repo Python lint clean for the changed file

Related: #37118 (anchor pruning must treat these overrides as references, or run after this repoint).

title: fix: profile README Projects omits public repos in the user's organisations; sort alphabetically
body:
## Problem

The profile README Projects block (added in GH#36913) lists only repositories owned by the personal account. Public repositories in organisations the user administers never appear (here, 9 repos across wpallstars, brandlight, essentials-com and flumberico). The owner also wants the list sorted alphabetically instead of by stars.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `gh api 'orgs/wpallstars/repos?type=public' --jq '.[] | select(.fork==false and .archived==false) | .name'`, then compare the result with the Projects block on https://github.com/marcusquinn

**Actual output:** five public repos (seoprostack, seoprocookieconsent, seoproanalytics, wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices, wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding), none of which appear in Projects. The same applies to brandlight, essentials-com and flumberico (9 repos in total).

**Cause:** `rg -n 'type=owner' .agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` shows that `_generate_projects` only queries `users/<user>/repos?type=owner`.

## Fix

In `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`:

- New `_list_profile_admin_orgs`: lists active orgs where the authenticated user is admin (GitHub records no repo creator, so admin is the proxy). It returns nothing when the profile user is not the authenticated user, and fails closed on API errors or malformed data.
- `_generate_projects`: also lists `orgs/<org>/repos?type=public` for those orgs. It excludes forks, archived and private repos, and org `.github` repos, and dedupes by URL. The list is sorted alphabetically by repo name, and org repos show `(org)` after the link. Any failure preserves the existing block.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` and `/bin/bash -n` are clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: 30/30 pass.
- Dry-run of `_refresh_projects_block` against the live README: 9 org repos added, alphabetical, idempotent; a stubbed `gh` failure preserves the block.

title: issue-triage-gate: repo admin with CONTRIBUTOR association labelled external-contributor + needs-maintainer-review
body:
## What happened

`issue-triage-gate-reusable.yml` (pinned at `88a58611e47951581292bdd7b65f2ed287f13da0` in a managed org repo) labelled an issue opened by the repository's **admin** with `external-contributor` and `needs-maintainer-review`. The run log says:

```
Author <owner> has role CONTRIBUTOR — applying triage gate
```

Live `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission` for that author returns `admin`.

The PR fixing that issue was then blocked by `full-loop-helper.sh merge`: `Merge blocked: linked issue #N still requires maintainer review`.

## Cause

The gate treats only `OWNER` and `MEMBER` associations as trusted and runs the live permission lookup only when `author_association === 'COLLABORATOR'`. GitHub reports `CONTRIBUTOR` (or `NONE`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`) for an org member whose membership is private, even when they hold admin on the repository, so the lookup never runs.

## Fix

Run the live write-level permission lookup for every association other than `OWNER`/`MEMBER` (or for every non-bot author), not only `COLLABORATOR`. Keep the existing fail-closed behaviour when the lookup errors.

Files: `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate-reusable.yml` (the `authorIsTrusted` block). Then bump the pinned ref in the caller template used by `aidevops sync-workflows --workflow issue-triage-gate`.

## Verification

- An issue opened by a repo admin whose org membership is private gets no `external-contributor` / `needs-maintainer-review` labels; log shows the permission lookup and the bypass.
- An issue opened by a read-only or non-collaborator account still gets both labels.

## Workaround used

Labels removed by hand on the affected issue after confirming live `admin` permission (write-authorized author normalization, `reference/auto-merge.md`).

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #21415 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #21415

**Parent issue:** #21415 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,source:conflict-feedback,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #21415 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#21415 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 21415 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #21415, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 21415 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 21415 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 21415 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 21415 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #21415 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #21415.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @vladimirdulov

title: session-count-helper reports 0 OpenCode sessions: runtime-registry pgrep pattern expects .opencode binary
body:
## What

`session-count-helper.sh list` reports `0 interactive` while about 25 OpenCode TUI sessions (`opencode --auto --agent Build+`) are running. Any session-count limit or warning that uses this helper is blind to OpenCode.

## Evidence (2026-11-07, macOS)

- `bash .agents/scripts/session-count-helper.sh list` printed `No interactive AI sessions detected` and `Total: 0 interactive | Threshold: 128`.
- At the same moment, `pgrep -fl opencode` listed about 25 processes whose command line is `opencode --auto --agent Build+` or `opencode --session ses_... --auto --agent Build+`, each started by `opencode-launcher-helper.sh --tabby-shell`.
- Earlier in the same session the helper reported 1, so the count is unreliable rather than always zero.

## Likely cause (verify first)

`.agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh` sets the OpenCode process pattern to `\.opencode` (around line 413) with pgrep mode `f` (around line 394). The comment says the binary runs as `.opencode`, but current TUI processes run as `opencode` with no leading dot, so `pgrep -f '\.opencode'` matches nothing. The pattern is used by `.agents/scripts/session-count-helper.sh` at lines 114-130 (count) and 199-213 (list).

## Files to change

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh`: OpenCode entries in the pgrep pattern array (~413), the pgrep mode array (~394) and possibly the exclusion pattern (~434, currently `(typescript-language-server|eslintServer|vscode-)|^node .*/bin/opencode`). Match both `opencode` and `.opencode` binaries without matching `opencode-launcher-helper.sh`, `opencode serve`, `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` or `opencode run` (headless, ~373).
- `.agents/scripts/session-count-helper.sh`: only if the pattern change alone is not enough.

## Out of scope

`Threshold: 128` comes from `get_max_sessions` (~67-81) reading the user's `safety.max_interactive_sessions` config. That is configuration, not a bug.

## Verification

1. With several OpenCode TUI sessions open, `bash .agents/scripts/session-count-helper.sh list` lists each `opencode --auto ...` process once and does not list launcher shells, `opencode serve` or `opencode run` workers.
2. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh .agents/scripts/session-count-helper.sh` is clean.
3. Run the existing tests for these scripts if any exist (`git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*session-count*' '.agents/scripts/tests/*runtime-registry*'`).

## Context

Found while designing OpenCode-to-OpenCode session messaging, which needs a reliable list of live sessions.

title: opencode-activity heartbeat files from dead processes are never pruned (372 files, ~15 live)
body:
## What

`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/opencode-activity/` keeps growing with heartbeat files from dead OpenCode processes. Nothing prunes them.

## Evidence (2026-11-07, macOS)

- The directory holds about 372 `<pid>-<instance>.json` files (1.4MB).
- About 15 of them belong to PIDs of currently running `opencode` processes (`pgrep -fl opencode`). The rest are from processes that have exited.

## Cause

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs` removes its own file only from `process.once("exit", ...)` (around line 206). Crashes, `SIGKILL`, closed terminals and host restarts skip that handler. The comment near line 193 notes that stale files for dead PIDs are ignored by the gate, but nothing deletes them.

## Impact

- Unbounded growth (small per file, but no cap).
- The archive idle gate (`.agents/scripts/opencode-db-idle-gate-lib.sh`, around lines 110-155) reads every `${pid}-*.json` for a holder PID. If a PID is reused, an old file reporting busy sessions can make the gate defer without cause.
- Planned session presence/messaging work will read this directory, so stale entries would show sessions that no longer exist.

## Proposed fix

When the heartbeat starts (in `installDbActivityHeartbeat` in `db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`), do a best-effort sweep of the directory. Delete a file only when its PID is not alive, or when it is alive but its process start identity does not match. Reuse `process-liveness.mjs` (`isOwnerProcessLive`, `processStartToken`) and `process-start-identity.mjs` rather than adding new liveness code. The heartbeat JSON (`snapshot()`, around lines 107-116) does not store a process start token today; add one so PID reuse can be detected. Never delete the current process's own file, and never block plugin start on the sweep.

## Files to change

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/db-activity-heartbeat.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-idle-gate-lib.sh`: only if the gate should also ignore files whose start token does not match.

## Verification

1. Start an OpenCode session with the updated plugin. Files for dead PIDs are removed and files for live PIDs remain (`fd -e json . ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/opencode-activity` before and after).
2. The existing archive idle-gate test still passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`.
3. Plugin lint/typecheck as configured for `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`.

title: t18886: OpenCode session bus: presence and session-to-session messages
body:
**Task ID:** `t18886` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `feat`

## Outcome

OpenCode session bus: presence and session-to-session messages

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

- Created: 2026-11-07, interactive session (owner-approved plan).
- Plan: `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md` (added by this task's PR). Related captures: #37145, #37146. Follow-up: #37157 (t18888, OpenCode 2 support).

## What

Add an OpenCode → OpenCode session bus to the aidevops OpenCode plugin:

1. **Presence:** every live interactive OpenCode root session publishes a ~1KB status record (title, handle, repo, worktree, branch, linked issue/PR, busy/idle/permission, current in-progress todo). `aidevops sessions list` (CLI) and the `aidevops_sessions` tool (`list`/`show`) show what every session is doing.
2. **Messages:** `send` (info), `ask` (expects reply), `reply`, `inbox`, `notify-when-idle` between sessions.
3. **Delivery:** busy recipient → appended to its next tool result (`tool.execute.after`); next user turn → synthetic part on the user message (`chat.message`); idle recipient + `ask`/reply-to-own-ask/requested idle notice → wake with `client.session.promptAsync` (owner decision 1a). TUI toast on arrival.
4. **Sidebar:** an optional "Messages" section in the right sidebar directly under "Prompts" (OpenCode 1.x `v1-tui/tui.tsx`), listing recent sent/received bus messages; disable with `AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES=false`. OpenCode 2 moved to #37157, because the V2 server plugin does not run the bus yet.
5. **Chat-app wiring (enablement only):** message `origin` field and an outbox so a later SimpleX/Matrix/Buzz gateway can list sessions, send to a live session as an untrusted external origin (never wakes), and collect replies from `outbox/<gateway>/`. Gateways themselves are out of scope.

## Why

Agents repeatedly ask the user to relay messages between parallel OpenCode sessions or to find out what another session is doing. The old mailbox (`mail-helper.sh`) never delivered to live sessions: 1,740 messages, all unread; recipients are folder/branch names, not sessions; no plugin delivery hook. A same-machine bus removes the human relay at negligible storage and context cost, and gives chat apps one contract for remote/mobile use of long-running OpenCode (and OpenCode server) sessions.

## How (as built)

- Storage under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/session-bus/` (override `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR`): `presence/`, `inbox/<session>/` with `delivered/`, `sent/<sender>/`, `subs/<session>/`, `outbox/<app>/`. Atomic temp+rename writes. Liveness is pid plus process start time, implemented in `session-bus-store.mjs`.
- Modules in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`: `session-bus-store.mjs` (storage, resolution, limits, framing; re-exports `session-bus-{files,presence-store,targets,messages,inbox,format}.mjs`), `session-bus.mjs` (presence and delivery runtime, 5s poll; uses `session-bus-{presence,identity,events,delivery,client}.mjs`), `session-bus-tool.mjs` (tool), `session-bus-cli.mjs` + `session-bus-cli-commands.mjs` (CLI), `tui-messages.mjs` (sidebar rows). Wired in `index.mjs` via `session-bus-plugin.mjs` (events, `chat.message`, `tool.execute.after`, tool registration) and `compaction.mjs` via `session-bus-compaction.mjs` (open asks). The split keeps each new file under the Qlty smell thresholds that the regression gate enforces.
- CLI: `aidevops sessions …` → `_main_dispatch_opencode_tools` in `aidevops.sh` → `.agents/scripts/session-bus-helper.sh` → `session-bus-cli.mjs`.
- Chat origin: `--origin chat:<app>:<channel>` (the brief's draft said `external:<name>`).
- Docs: `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`, Messages note in `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`. No `.agents/AGENTS.md` pointer: the file is at its 24,000-byte ratchet, and the tool description carries the "do not ask the user to relay" rule.
- Old mailbox untouched (retirement is a separate owner decision).

### Files Scope

title: large-file gate: report and retry debt-issue links instead of 'none created'
body:
## What

The large-file simplification gate can hold an issue with `needs-simplification` while its comment says **"Simplification issues: none created"**. Once the label is applied, the gate never retries linking the debt issue. The parent then shows no visible dependency, even when a debt issue exists or a lookup only failed transiently.

## Evidence

- #36916 gate comment (2026-11-06T17:43Z) says "none created" for `profile-readme-helper.sh` and `audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`.
- An open debt issue already existed for `profile-readme-helper.sh` (#21415, since 2026-04-27; now superseded by #37143).
- Working out the real blocker took a manual search of `file-size-debt` issues.

## Reproducer

Live case: `gh issue view 36916 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --comments`. The "Large File Simplification Gate" comment says "none created". Meanwhile `gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label file-size-debt --state open --search profile-readme-helper` returns #37143 (previously #21415, open since 2026-04-27). The parent has kept `needs-simplification` since 2026-11-06T17:43Z and the comment has never been updated.

## Root cause (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`)

- `_large_file_gate_create_debt_issue`, lines ~807-809: when the dedup lookup fails (rc=2), it returns 0 with empty stdout ("deferring filing to next cycle").
- Lines ~841-844: the reopen path for a closed, still-oversized debt issue returns 0 with empty stdout, even when the reopen succeeds.
- `_large_file_gate_apply`, lines ~888-905: empty stdout is rendered as "none created".
- `_large_file_gate_precheck_labels`, lines ~120-123: already-labelled issues short-circuit (return 2), so the deferred "next cycle" never happens unless `force_recheck` re-evaluation runs.

## How

1. Reopen path: print `#NNN (reopened)` after a successful `_large_file_gate_reopen_debt_issue`.
2. Lookup deferral: print a pending marker (for example `pending (lookup deferred)`). The comment then says the link is pending instead of "none created".
3. In the re-evaluation path (`_reevaluate_simplification_labels`, force_recheck=true), when the gate still applies and the existing gate comment has no `#NNN` debt reference, re-run debt-issue linking and update the idempotent comment.

Reference pattern: the existing idempotent comment helper `_gh_idempotent_comment` and the `#NNN (existing)` output convention in the same file.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`
- Existing suites: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-*.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh`.
- Expected: a gated issue with an existing open or closed-and-reopened debt issue gets a comment naming that issue. A deferred lookup is shown as pending and is linked on the next re-evaluation.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` (1268 lines; under the large-file threshold)

## What and why

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` evaluates the t2449 worker-briefed trust gate through `_merge_worker_briefed_trust_gate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh:582`) → `worker_briefed_trust_verdict` (`:528`), which reads the PR body with `gh_pr_view ... --json labels,isDraft,headRefOid,body`. Inside a supervisor-pulse session the environment sets `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE=1`, `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_TTL=3600` and a cross-cycle `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DIR`. The trust gate does not set `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DISABLE=1`, and `gh-write-helper.sh pr edit` does not invalidate the cached repo#PR object. After a supervisor repaired a worker PR body, the merge gate kept reading the pre-edit body for up to an hour. It then failed with the generic `Merge blocked by t2449: trust metadata unavailable (t2449)`.

The comment at `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:265` already says mutation-sensitive merge gates must bypass this cache. Other full-loop reads already do: `full-loop-helper-readiness.sh:414`, `full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh:136,196` and `full-loop-helper-evidence.sh:33`.

## Evidence (2026-11-07, supervisor pulse, v3.39.134 runtime bundle)

- I edited a worker PR body with `gh-write-helper.sh pr edit N --body-file ...`. Native `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh pr view N --json body` and `gh api repos/.../pulls/N` both returned the new body.
- The `gh` shim (`pr view` REST rewrite) and `gh_pr_view` still returned the old body. The file `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-pr-view-cache/<owner>_<repo>__N.json` was written 2 minutes before the edit.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge N SLUG --squash` failed twice with `trust metadata unavailable (t2449)`.
- `env AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DISABLE=1 full-loop-helper.sh merge N SLUG --squash` passed all gates and merged on the first attempt.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh:582-600` (`_merge_worker_briefed_trust_gate`): run the verdict with `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DISABLE=1` (the subshell already isolates globals). Follow `full-loop-helper-evidence.sh:33`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh:106-134` plus the PR edit/merge write path (`gh_pr_edit_safe` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` and/or the `pr:edit` branch of `.agents/scripts/gh`): after a successful PR edit, delete the repo#PR cache file `_rest_pr_view_cache_path REPO N`. Also delete the matching exact-argv snapshots if they are cheap to find; otherwise rely on the gate bypass.
- Optional: in `worker_briefed_trust_verdict`, make the denial reason say whether the PR view failed or the explicit identity was ambiguous, not the generic "trust metadata unavailable".

### Verification

- Extend the existing worker-briefed trust suite (`rg -l "worker_briefed_trust_verdict" .agents/scripts/tests`). With a warm stale cache entry holding an ambiguous body and a live body holding one identity, the full-loop gate must allow.
- `shellcheck` clean on touched files.

title: Worker PR bodies still reach GitHub with dual For #child/#parent identities after GH#36877
body:
## What and why

GH#36877 (PR #36879) added `_gh_validate_pr_worker_identity` (`.agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:185`). It rejects `origin:worker` PR bodies that declare more than one explicit `For/Ref #N` identity. Worker PRs created on v3.39.131 and v3.39.133 runners still reached GitHub with two standalone lines, `For #<child>` and `For #<parent>`. The deterministic merge pass then logs `_extract_pr_work_issue: ... ambiguous explicit issue identities — no merge association` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1847`) on every cycle. Ready, green PRs stay open until a supervisor edits the body by hand. One PR was skipped for about 9 hours.

## Evidence (2026-11-07, one managed private product repo)

- Two non-draft `origin:worker` collaborator PRs with all checks green each had `For #<child>` and `For #<parent>` (a parent-task or consolidated parent) on consecutive standalone lines. They were created by a Linux runner on v3.39.131 and v3.39.133.
- The local pulse.log had 49 `ambiguous explicit issue identities` lines. A supervisor moved the parent reference under `## Related`, and both PRs then merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`.
- The create path that skipped the guard is unknown. Possibilities: raw `gh pr create` through the PATH shim (`.agents/scripts/gh` runs `_shim_validate_pr_closing_keywords` but may not run the explicit-identity check), creation before the `origin:worker` label was applied, or a remote runner with a stale deploy.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh` (`pr:create` / `pr:edit` handling near `_shim_validate_pr_closing_keywords`) or its policy lib (`.agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh`): run `_gh_validate_pr_worker_identity` for worker-origin bodies on raw `gh pr create|edit`. Treat the body as worker-origin when it carries `<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->` or the run is headless. Prefer normalizing: keep the standalone `For #N` that matches the dispatched issue or branch `ghNNNN`, and move the others under `## Related`. Fail closed only if no target can be chosen.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:185`: reuse the shared parser. Do not add a third copy.
- Confirm the explicit-identity case against `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh:393` and extend that suite for the raw-shim path.

### Verification

- A raw `gh pr create` (shim test mode) with a worker-origin body containing `For #A` and `For #B` is normalized or rejected. A normalized body passes `_extract_pr_work_issue <pr> <repo> explicit` with exactly one identity.
- Existing explicit-association and worker-briefed suites still pass; `shellcheck` clean.

title: t18887: feat: OpenCode browse support (install via setup/update, lazy MCP, routing docs)
body:
**Task ID:** `t18887` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-11-08 | **Started:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive`

## Outcome

feat: OpenCode browse support (install via setup/update, lazy MCP, routing docs)

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add first-class support for OpenCode browse (the `browse` CLI + Chrome Web Store extension `mfnicocicmmlkpjnaffgihfjhdgjkdjg`, installer `https://opencode.ai/browse/install`). It drives the user's existing Chromium-family browser through deterministic Playwright code, with handoffs, site-secret typing, allowlists, recordings and network capture.

## Why

aidevops currently tells agents that the user's everyday logged-in tab cannot be driven and routes to a dedicated-profile CDP launch. browse is an officially supported, extension-paired route into the user's real browser with explicit tab lending, per-session allowlists and human handoffs. Setup/update should install it automatically where a supported browser exists.

## How

Evidence from `browse` 0.0.15 (`browse --help`, `browse skill`, isolated-HOME probe of `browse install`):

- Installer `--no-setup` downloads a checksum-verified binary to `${XDG_BIN_HOME:-~/.local/bin}/browse`; `browse install --no-open --no-wait -a <agent|none>` configures agents and pairing; `browse mcp` is the stdio MCP server.
- Paths follow `XDG_{CONFIG,DATA,STATE,CACHE}_HOME/browse`. aidevops OpenCode sessions redirect `XDG_DATA_HOME` per project, so the relay token (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/browse/relay-token`) would differ per project. Precedent for dropping the redirect: `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-init.sh` `run_stable_mkcert`.

Files:

- NEW `.agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh` — `detect` (supported Chromium browsers), `install` (verified download, `--no-setup`, then `browse install -a none --no-modify-path`), `status`, `mcp` (launcher: drop aidevops per-session `XDG_DATA_HOME`, refuse headless/worker runtimes), `run -- <args>` (same stable env for CLI use).
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh` — `_setup_browser_tools_opencode_browse` from `setup_browser_tools`; install/update when a supported browser is detected; print Web Store + pairing steps.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs` — lazy `browse` registry entry (activation agent `opencode-browse`, `browse_*` tools) using the helper launcher; model on the `chrome-devtools`/`playwright` entries.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/agent-mcp-tools.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh`, `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-agents.sh`, `.agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py` (`LAZY_MCPS`).
- NEW `.agents/tools/browser/opencode-browse.md`; EDIT `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md` decision tree ("use my logged-in tab"), `.agents/subagent-index.toon`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh
- setup.sh
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/agent-mcp-tools.mjs
- .agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh
- .agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-agents.sh
- .agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py
- .agents/tools/browser/opencode-browse.md
- .agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md
- .agents/subagent-index.toon

## Acceptance

- `aidevops update`/`setup.sh --non-interactive` installs or refreshes `browse` when Chrome/Edge/Brave/Arc/Chromium/Vivaldi is present, never blocks waiting for pairing, and skips cleanly otherwise.
- OpenCode exposes `browse` via `aidevops_mcp connect browse` / `@opencode-browse` without eager loading.
- One relay token is shared across projects (launcher drops the per-session `XDG_DATA_HOME`).
- Headless/worker runtimes cannot drive the user's browser through the launcher.
- Docs route "use my real/logged-in browser tab" to browse when installed and paired; Playwright remains the default.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh .agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`
- `opencode-browse-helper.sh status` and a live `opencode-browse-helper.sh run -- execute --rm 'return 1+1'` against a paired Chrome.

title: t18888: OpenCode 2 support for the session bus: run the bus from v2.mjs and add the s...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18888` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~1d`
**Logged:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

OpenCode 2 support for the session bus: run the bus from v2.mjs and add the sidebar Messages section

**Blocked by:** `t18886`

## Done when

- [ ] V2 root sessions appear in `aidevops sessions list` with repo, branch and state, and disappear when their process dies.
- [ ] A V2 session can `send`, `ask` and `reply` with V1 sessions; an `ask` to an idle V2 session wakes it, or the PR documents which V2 channel is missing and how messages arrive instead.
- [ ] The V2 sidebar shows the Messages section under Prompts; `AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES=false` hides it.
- [ ] Headless V2 processes publish read-only presence and get no `aidevops_sessions` tool.
- [ ] Regression: V1 sessions behave as before (V1 session-bus tests pass; V1 sidebar unchanged), and a session open in both a V1 and a V2 process gets each message exactly once.
- [ ] Negative: a V2 session never wakes for `info` or chat-origin messages, and `send` to a headless V2 session is refused.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- V1 reference wiring: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` creates the bus at 446 (`createSessionBus({ client, directory, kind })`, `session-bus.mjs:551`), registers the tool at 467 (`if (sessionBus.messageable) …`), and calls `sessionBus.chatMessage` (741), `sessionBus.toolAfter` (793) and `sessionBus.handleEvent` (838).
- V2 server plugin: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs` builds tools at 367 (`createSchemaGatedTools`), adds them to the V2 editor at 459 (`addV1ToolsToV2Editor`), and feeds events at 274 and 550 (`handleEvent`). Add the bus there. Unknown until verified: which V2 hooks can append to a tool result or a user message, and whether the V2 client exposes `session.promptAsync` and `tui.showToast`. If a channel has no V2 equivalent, deliver through the remaining channels and record the gap in the PR.
- V2 TUI: follow `setupPromptsSlot` (`v2-plugin/tui.mjs:303`; slot registration `tui-prompts.mjs:152`, `prepend: "sidebar.content"`). Reuse `tui-messages.mjs` (`messageRows`, `rootSessionID`, `isMessagesEnabled`, `MESSAGES_POLL_MS`) so V1 and V2 show the same rows. Place it after Prompts.
- Keep `session-bus-store.mjs` unchanged unless V2 needs a new process `kind`; `processKind` is at `session-bus.mjs:38`.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: create the bus, register the tool, connect the hooks.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs`: add the Messages slot after Prompts.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-messages.mjs`: add a V2 slot setup next to the shared row builder, if that is the cleanest home (as `tui-prompts.mjs` does for Prompts).
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs` or a new focused test only if slot order needs a regression check (pattern: lines 117–131).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session-bus.md` and `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`: drop the "OpenCode 1.x only" scope notes.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `aidevops sessions` (`session-bus-cli.mjs`), the `aidevops_sessions` tool (`session-bus-tool.mjs`), the V1 sidebar (`v1-tui/tui.tsx` via `tui-messages.mjs`) and compaction (`compaction.mjs` `getSessionBusState`) all read the bus files. They need no change: V2 sessions write the same records.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the only new writer is the bus instance created in `v2.mjs`, which writes through `session-bus-store.mjs` (presence, inbox claims, sent copies, subscriptions, outbox), the same code V1 uses.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-session-bus.mjs` (store, runtime, tool, CLI, V1 rows) and `tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs:117-131` (V2 slot registration pattern). Runtime path: `aidevops sessions list` plus a live V2 session.
- **Schemas/config:** no schema change. Record `v: 1` stays. `AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES` and `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` keep their meaning.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/`. `v2.mjs`, `v2-plugin/tui.mjs` and `tui-messages.mjs` are already in the freshness list in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh:317-343`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** no stored data changes. V2 writes the same `v: 1` records into the directory layout that V1 already creates (`session-bus-store.mjs` `busRoot`), so nothing is migrated or backfilled.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** presence is removed on `session.deleted` and process exit and swept by `list` when the pid is dead. Rollback is reverting the `v2.mjs` and `v2-plugin/tui.mjs` edits; V2 sessions then simply stop appearing.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read the installed V2 host's plugin types (locate them with `fd` under the V2 install; do not guess paths) and record which hooks can append to a user message or a tool result, and whether the V2 client has `session.promptAsync`, `session.status` and `tui.showToast`.
2. Decide the delivery channels for V2 from step 1. If one is missing, keep the others and note the gap in the PR and in `reference/session-bus.md`.
3. In `v2.mjs`, create the bus once per process next to the existing tool setup (around 367), add `aidevops_sessions` to the tool set when `sessionBus.messageable`, and route events and hooks to `handleEvent`, `chatMessage` and `toolAfter` as `index.mjs` does.
4. In `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`, register a Messages slot after `setupPromptsSlot(api)` (line 303) that renders `messageRows` for the current root session every `MESSAGES_POLL_MS`.
5. Run the plugin tests, then the live check under Verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** V1 and V2 processes can hold the same session. Delivery already claims by rename (`session-bus-store.mjs`), so only one process delivers each message. Keep using the store API and do not write files directly.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored data changes, so rollback is a code revert. Messages already queued stay valid for V1.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** V1 and V2 plugins read and write the same `v: 1` records. A V2 process must not start a second bus in the same process if V1 hooks are also loaded; check the existing V1/V2 load guard in `v2.mjs` before wiring.
- **Idempotency/retry:** presence writes are idempotent, and wakes are rolled back on failure (`session-bus.mjs` wake path), so a retried wake does not double-deliver.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the V2 client lacks `promptAsync`, wakes fail and messages wait for the next turn; the runtime logs the failure through `warn()`. A crash leaves undelivered files, which any process delivers when the session resumes.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tui-messages.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-tui-prompts.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`
- `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md`
- `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus-v2.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`

_Integration scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-08): added `session-bus-v2.mjs` for the V2 client/event adapter (OpenCode 2.0.18 plugin ctx has `session.synthetic`/`session.get` but no `promptAsync`, `status` or `tui.showToast`, and events use `data` with `session.execution.*`), keeping `v2.mjs` wiring small, plus its focused test. Same bus store API, no format change._

_Deploy scope recovery (worker, 2026-11-08): `v2.mjs` now imports the new `session-bus-v2.mjs`, so it joins the core-plugin freshness list in `agent-deploy.sh` (one line), as the other session-bus modules did in t18886._

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs
```

- **Runtime evidence:** run an OpenCode 2 host (`aidevops opencode-sandbox` installs versions in isolation). With `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` pointing at a scratch directory, start one V2 session and one V1 session. `aidevops sessions list` shows both. A V1 `ask` to the idle V2 session wakes it, and its reply reaches V1. The V2 sidebar shows the Messages rows under Prompts.
- **Test setup note:** an isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` that loads the plugin from a repo worktree cannot resolve `@opencode-ai/plugin`, so no tools register (`tool-schema.mjs` logs `V1 schemas unavailable`). Link the deployed plugin's `node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin` into the worktree plugin directory for the test, then remove the link (it is gitignored).
- **Surface mapping:** `npm test` covers the shared store and runtime (concurrency, idempotency, partial-failure rollback) and the V1 regression criterion. `node --check` covers `v2.mjs` syntax. The live V1↔V2 run covers the `v2.mjs` writer path, the V2 presence, messaging and wake criteria, the headless criterion (start one `opencode run` and confirm it is listed read-only with `list --all`), and mixed-version compatibility. A V2 TUI session covers `v2-plugin/tui.mjs` and the sidebar criterion; the owner checks it visually.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. Changes stay inside the plugin and its docs.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t18888 V2 session bus`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required (plugin-only change)

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no change to message format, limits, trust framing or storage layout; V1 behaviour unchanged; no chat-app gateway work (Phase 3); old mailbox untouched.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive owner session of t18886 (marcusquinn).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-08
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (t18886 build, GH#37149)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** t18886 shipped the session bus (presence, `aidevops_sessions`, `aidevops sessions`, delivery, wakes, V1 sidebar) for OpenCode 1.x. GH#37149 also asked for the sidebar "Messages" section in V2. The V2 server plugin does not run the bus, so a V2 sidebar alone would always be empty. The V2 part was split out into this task.

## What

OpenCode 2 sessions take part in the session bus the same way OpenCode 1.x sessions do:

1. The V2 server plugin (`v2.mjs`) runs `createSessionBus`: it publishes root-session presence, polls inboxes, delivers messages and wakes idle sessions.
2. V2 sessions get the `aidevops_sessions` tool when the process is messageable (TUI, `serve`, ACP).
3. The V2 TUI (`v2-plugin/tui.mjs`) shows the **Messages** sidebar section directly under **Prompts**, with the same rows and the same `AIDEVOPS_TUI_MESSAGES=false` switch as V1.

## Why

Without this, V2 sessions are invisible to `aidevops sessions list` and cannot send or receive messages, so agents in V2 still ask the user to relay between sessions.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The V2 host exposes different hook and client surfaces from V1. Delivery needs equivalents of `chat.message`, `tool.execute.after`, `session.promptAsync` and `tui.showToast`, and those must be verified against the V2 host before wiring.

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #36916 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#36916 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 36916 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #36916, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 36916 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 36916 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 36916 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 36916 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #36916 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #36916.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Problem

The profile README publication job still retains one detached worktree per run on macOS after #36543, #36715 and #36741 closed. On the maintainer host, 58 `<profile-repo>-profile-readme-*` worktrees exist under the worktree base (oldest 2026-10-23, newest 2026-11-06), and the per-run sweep never retires any of them.
