title: consolidated: stop profile publication worktree leaks and recovery starvation
body:
_Supersedes #36916 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Stop profile README publication from leaking detached worktrees and prevent backlog recovery from starving publication, while preserving guarded recovery and ownership safety.

## Why

After #36543, #36715 and #36741, the macOS launchd `sh.aidevops.profile-readme-update` job using the `legacy-guards` manager accumulated 58 publication worktrees as of 2026-11-06 (oldest 2026-10-23); the sweep retired zero and preserved an increasing count for guarded recovery. Measure with `fd -t d -d 1 '<profile-repo>-profile-readme-' "${AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR:-$HOME/Git/_worktrees}" | wc -l`. Logs showed `restore-proof:registration-changed` (58 occurrences), `producer:evidence-unavailable; cause=fingerprint-unavailable` (4), lifecycle `retirement-refused status=coverage-gap` (enrolled without a registered owner), and 52 canonical Git guard probe timeouts in the marker writer leaving intent but no marker.

Per @marcusquinn, recovery held the overlap lock for hours, causing hourly refreshes to skip. Other recovery errors included `producer:evidence-unavailable; cause=stderr/unclassified` and `producer:base-import-failed; stage=base-import; exit=42`. A subsequent update failed before publishing when ownership observe raised `TimeoutExpired`, retaining a worktree whose creation metadata registration failed; lifecycle reported `not-enrolled`. Backlog and creation failures can reinforce each other. By 2026-11-07 the sweep preserved 62 trees, one run was SIGTERM'd, another held the lock over an hour in `session-time-interval-engine.py --period profile --all-dirs`, and only one publication succeeded in 27 hours. This was found while diagnosing #36913 and is not caused by it.

## How

- Investigate and fix guarded current-run cleanup, prior-worktree eligibility, sweep and marker creation in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-publication-lib.sh:244`, `:356`, `:404`, `:485`, and `:627` (publication functions moved from `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh` after the original brief); integration calls are in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh:1196`.
- Investigate `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:906` and its archive/restore-proof path for registration changes, together with `worktree-helper.sh` lifecycle `retire-enrolled-only` coverage-gap and `shared-worktree-create.sh` `worktree_create_registered` owner PID/session registration. Resolve the canonical Git guard timeout affecting the marker's `git rev-parse` without weakening safety; intent without a marker must remain safely handled.
- Per @marcusquinn, bound recovery per run by both count and time and continue to refresh even with a large retained backlog; cover publication worktree enrollment or a cheap ownership observe path so a slow backlog does not cause creation failure and another unenrolled worktree. Preserve unsafe or unverifiable worktrees for guarded recovery, rather than deleting them to meet a count.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` with sweep, recovery, registration/marker failure and backlog cases, including more than 10 retained trees. Test the actual publication path and maintain guard invariants.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A completed clean publication worktree whose HEAD is already on `origin/<default>` is retired in the same run or the next sweep; unsafe or unproven trees remain protected.
- [ ] Recovery count and elapsed time are bounded per run; a fixture with more than 10 retained worktrees demonstrates refresh publishes within one run.
- [ ] Publication creation handles enrollment/observe under backlog without repeatedly retaining unenrolled worktrees; registration changes and marker probe failures are handled safely.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` passes for sweep/recovery cases on CI and macOS.
- [ ] On a macOS host, two consecutive `profile-readme-helper.sh update` runs leave zero `*-profile-readme-*` worktrees when eligible and log `retired N earlier worktree(s)` with N > 0 when an eligible backlog exists. Report macOS availability and evidence rather than inventing host results.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-publication-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`

## Context & Decisions

- @marcusquinn supplied the original symptoms and the additions requiring bounded recovery, non-starvation, and robust enrollment/observe. The large-file gate was attributed to #37143, but the later automated gate-cleared comment supersedes the claim that the task must wait for simplification. The separate gate reporting gap is not part of this fix.
- @alex-solovyev recorded the automated simplification-gate clearance: references now satisfy the scoped-range bypass or files are below the threshold. Do not reinstate the previous hold solely on the old comment.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: Recurring flake: bounded-operation start test reports post_exit_descendants_terminated under full suite (t18689 regression)
body:
## What

`tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:47` still fails intermittently under the full plugin suite. This is the same flake as t18689 / #34573, which PR #34579 was meant to fix.

The test "start returns control and explicit progress reaches a private terminal receipt" (line 26) runs `node -e "console.log('AIDEVOPS_PROGRESS: phase-one'); setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 80)"`. That command has no children, but the receipt sometimes reports `post_exit_descendants_terminated: true`:

```text
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
true !== false
    at TestContext.<anonymous> (.../tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:47:12)
```

## Evidence (2026-11-08, macOS, node v26.12.0)

- Failed once during `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` pre-push validation: `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`, running inside an `aidevops_bounded_operation` alongside other host load.
- Passed on the same tree twice under the full suite: one standalone `npm test` and one earlier `commit-and-pr` validator run.
- Passed when the file ran alone: `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` (exit 0).
- The failing branch did not touch any bounded-operation module.

## Likely cause (inferred, not proven)

In `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs`, the child `exit` handler (about 218–227) calls `terminateSurvivors()`, which sets `postExitDescendantsTerminated = true`. It does so when `tracker.nestedTargets(snapshot).length` is non-zero or `tracker.ownGroupMembers(snapshot) > 1`. `ownedTreeDrained(...)` (about line 231) can call `terminateSurvivors` too. Under load, the `ps` snapshot may still list the exited child (unreaped or zombie), or a transient process in the supervisor's group. Either can count as a survivor. PR #34579 changed only `survivorSnapshot` in the same file.

## How

1. Reproduce under load: run `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` in a loop while the CPU is busy, or run several test files concurrently. Count how often line 47 fails.
2. Log the snapshot entries that `survivorSnapshot` / `ownGroupMembers` count when the flag flips. Find the process that counts as a survivor.
3. Fix the classification in `bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` or `bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs`: exclude the exited command identity, zombies (`stat` Z), and the tracker's own `ps` invocation. Do not loosen the assertion. The receipt field is user-facing liveness evidence (see `bounded-operation-tool.mjs:17`).

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs` (exit handler, `terminateSurvivors`, drain loop)
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-process-tree.mjs` (`ownGroupMembers`, `nestedTargets`, snapshot parsing)
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:26-50` (failing test; keep its assertions)
- Reference: PR #34579 (prior fix), #34573 (prior issue)

## Verification

- The test passes in at least 20 consecutive full-suite runs under concurrent load, where it previously failed intermittently.
- `bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:54` (forked survivor reports `true`) and the completion-mode case at `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:403` still pass, so real survivors are still reported.
- `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` exits 0.

title: commit-and-pr: run the public-diff privacy scan before validators so local-path leaks fail fast
body:
## What

Make `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` run the public-repo privacy scan before the long validators and test suites. Today the privacy guard runs only in the pre-push hook. A single local path in a committed doc therefore fails the run only after the whole validator and pre-push test pass.

## Evidence (2026-11-08, macOS, interactive session)

- The `commit-and-pr` run for GH#37149 took ~512s. The npm validators and pre-push suites all passed (tool-install 107/0, plugin 90/0). Then the push failed with:

title: fix: signing setup skips the interactive key in allowed_signers when headless-setup ran first
body:
# fix: `signing setup` skips the interactive key in allowed_signers when headless-setup ran first

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `signing headless-setup commit signing worker failures` → 0 hits — no relevant stored lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch the allowed_signers append logic in last 48h (last change to the file is `c1d03ee92`, ssh-agent persistence, unrelated); `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 claimed issues
- [x] File refs verified: `signing-setup.sh:212-229`, `:290-317`, `:235`, `:330-333`, `tests/test-signing-setup.sh` all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `standard` — the primary append fix is deterministic, but reconciling it with the existing headless replace path is an unresolved design decision
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — single-file change, a seed would save no exploration

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-08
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While completing SSH signing setup on a NixOS host, `aidevops signing check` reported all-OK, but the configured interactive signing key was absent from `allowed_signers`, so local signature verification could not work.

## What

Three corrections in `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh`:

1. `cmd_setup` must guarantee the public key it configures as `user.signingkey` is present in `~/.ssh/allowed_signers` for the Git email, including when a line for that email already exists from `cmd_headless_setup`.
2. `cmd_headless_setup` must stop deleting every line for the Git email when it refreshes its own entry, so a headless key rotation cannot remove the interactive principal.
3. The post-setup guidance that tells users to add `agent-start` to a shell profile or cron must reflect that pulse and the headless runtime already self-heal a stale agent.

## Reproducer

Confirmed on a live host (Linux/NixOS, aidevops v3.39.132) on 2026-11-07, following the order the script's own "Next steps" output implies. Works on any host with no prior `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.

```bash
# Preconditions: git user.email set; ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub exists; no allowed_signers yet.
rm -f ~/.ssh/allowed_signers                 # clean slate for the reproduction

aidevops signing headless-setup              # appends "<git-email> <headless-key>"
aidevops signing setup                       # prints "[INFO] Email already in allowed_signers file"
aidevops signing check                       # reports every item OK

# Expected: both the headless key and user.signingkey appear.
# Actual: the key named by user.signingkey is absent.
rg -o 'AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI[A-Za-z0-9+/]{10}' ~/.ssh/allowed_signers
rg -o 'AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI[A-Za-z0-9+/]{10}' "$(git config --global user.signingkey)"
```

Observed sequence:

1. `aidevops signing headless-setup` appends `<git-email> <headless-key>` to `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
2. `aidevops signing setup` prints `[INFO] Email already in allowed_signers file` and does **not** append the interactive key.
3. `aidevops signing check` then reports every item OK, including `[OK] Allowed signers file exists`.

Actual file contents after both commands — exactly two ed25519 keys, with the configured interactive key missing:

```text
AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIPNr4j5hXQw   headless key (~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub)
AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIMnXVft9/hT   aidevops maintainer trusted key
```

Meanwhile `git config --global user.signingkey` is `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, whose key material is `AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIJC1M4KPupAeMa…`. Consequence: `git log --show-signature` cannot verify the user's own commits, and no command reports a problem.

Control proving the mechanism works when the key *is* present — signing and verifying with the headless key succeeds:

```text
$ ssh-keygen -Y sign -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing -n git probe.txt
$ cat probe.txt | ssh-keygen -Y verify -f ~/.ssh/allowed_signers -I <git-email> -n git -s probe.txt.sig
Good "git" signature for <git-email> with ED25519 key SHA256:j/LUFybOPnfyJGRDGr/rcA/XvZ5a+lpGJEp+aEPqMBY
```

## Root cause

`cmd_setup` guards the append with an **email**-presence test only (`signing-setup.sh:215`):

```bash
if [[ ! -f "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" ]] || ! grep -q "$git_email" "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
```

`cmd_headless_setup` already does the correct two-stage check — email first, then key material (`signing-setup.sh:293-309`):

```bash
if [[ ! -f "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" ]] || ! grep -qF "$git_email" "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
	echo "$git_email $key_content" >>"$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE"
else
	if ! grep -qF "$key_content" "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
		...
```

`cmd_setup` is missing that second stage. Because `headless-setup` seeds the email first, the interactive key is silently skipped.

Two adjacent problems in the same code:

- **Replace path is too broad.** `cmd_headless_setup:300-305` builds the new file with `grep -vF "$git_email"`, dropping *every* line for that principal, then appends only the headless key. `allowed_signers` legitimately supports multiple lines per principal, one per key. Once defect 1 is fixed, a headless key rotation would delete the interactive entry.
- **Unanchored, non-fixed matching.** Lines 215 and 223 use `grep -q` without `-F`, so an address containing regex metacharacters can match incorrectly. Lines 293/298/312 already use `-F`.

## Why

A silent, self-reported-healthy verification gap. `check` prints success while local verification is impossible, so the condition is undiscoverable without manually reading `allowed_signers`. It hits every user who runs `headless-setup` before `setup` — which is the order implied by the headless "Next steps" output and by the quick-start block in `reference/git-signing.md:25-30`.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The `cmd_setup` append fix has an exact write surface and mechanical verification, but the headless replace path requires deciding how to reconcile multi-key-per-principal entries with key-rotation cleanup — a semantic decision the brief does not resolve.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:212-220` — add the key-presence stage to `cmd_setup`, modelled on `cmd_headless_setup:293-309`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:296-309` — narrow the replace so it removes only lines carrying the headless key, not all lines for the email
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:215,223` — use `grep -qF` for consistency with the headless path
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:235` and `:330-333` — correct the `agent-start` guidance
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh` — regression coverage for the ordering

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `signing-setup.sh` is the only writer of `$HOME/.ssh/allowed_signers` (verified: `rg 'ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE|ssh/allowed_signers' .agents/ -g '!*.md'`). Readers are Git via `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` (set at `:228` and `:317`), `signing-setup.sh:481` in the verify path, and `aidevops-cli/aidevops-status-lib.sh:349`, which only tests existence. `setup/modules/source-access.sh:120` passes its own unrelated path via `-c`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `cmd_setup:216,224`, `cmd_headless_setup:294,303,313`. Both are append-or-replace against the same file.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh` (323 lines) sandboxes `HOME` to a `mktemp -d` tree and shims `git`/`ssh-add` on PATH (see `:7-60`). It currently has no `allowed_signers` coverage — `rg 'allowed_signers' tests/test-signing-setup.sh` returns nothing. Extend this existing harness; do not build new infrastructure.
- **Schemas/config:** none; `allowed_signers` is OpenSSH's own line-oriented format (`principal keytype keydata`).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh` is the deployed copy. Edit the repo file and redeploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive`; never edit the deployed path.
- **Migrations/backfills:** existing hosts already have an incomplete `allowed_signers`. Re-running `aidevops signing setup` after the fix must repair them, because the append becomes key-conditional rather than email-conditional. State this in the PR body.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** the replace path at `:300-305` writes via `mktemp` then `mv`; preserve that atomic swap.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace the `cmd_setup` guard so the key is appended whenever that exact key material is absent, regardless of other entries for the email.

   oldString (`signing-setup.sh:215-220`):

   ```bash
   	if [[ ! -f "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" ]] || ! grep -q "$git_email" "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
   		echo "$git_email $key_content" >>"$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE"
   		_print_ok "Added $git_email to $ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE"
   	else
   		_print_info "Email already in allowed_signers file"
   	fi
   ```

   newString:

   ```bash
   	# GH#NNNN: an entry for this email may already exist from headless-setup.
   	# Match on key material, not just the principal, so the interactive signing
   	# key is never skipped. allowed_signers allows one line per key per principal.
   	if [[ ! -f "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" ]] || ! grep -qF "$key_content" "$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
   		echo "$git_email $key_content" >>"$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE"
   		_print_ok "Added $git_email interactive signing key to $ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE"
   	else
   		_print_info "Interactive signing key already in allowed_signers file"
   	fi
   ```

2. Change `grep -q "$TRUSTED_EMAIL"` at `:223` to `grep -qF "$TRUSTED_EMAIL"`, matching `:312`.

3. Decide and implement the narrowed replace in `cmd_headless_setup:296-309`. The entry to remove is the stale *headless* line, identified by the headless key's own comment (`aidevops-headless-signing`, set at `:274`) or by retaining every line whose key material differs from both the old and new headless key. Preserve the `mktemp` + `mv` atomic swap and the existing `_print_ok "Updated …"` message. Record the chosen rule in a comment.

4. Correct the guidance strings. At `:330-333` the current text is:

   ```bash
   	echo "  2. Add agent-start to your shell profile or cron environment:"
   	echo "     aidevops signing agent-start"
   ```

   Pulse and the headless runtime already rerun `agent-start` when `agent.env` names an unreachable agent — documented at `reference/git-signing.md:54-58` and surfaced by `cmd_check:163` ("Pulse restarts it on its next cycle"). Reword to state that no shell-profile hook is required and that `agent-start` is for restoring the agent immediately. Apply the equivalent correction to the `cmd_setup` next-steps block at `:235` if it carries the same claim.

5. Add regression coverage to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh` using the existing sandbox: generate an `id_ed25519.pub` in `$TEST_HOME/.ssh`, pre-seed `allowed_signers` with `<email> <headless-key>`, run the script's `setup`, then assert both key blobs are present. Add a second case asserting a headless key refresh leaves the interactive line intact.

6. Run `shellcheck .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh`, then the test file, then `linters-local.sh --changed`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** `cmd_setup` appends with `>>`, which is a single small write; the replace path must keep `mktemp` + `mv`. Do not introduce a read-modify-write without the temp-file swap.
- **Migration/rollback:** hosts with an incomplete file are repaired by re-running `setup`; no destructive migration. Rollback is reverting the commit — already-appended lines stay valid and harmless.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** a file written by the old code remains readable; the new check only adds a missing line. Duplicate-key lines must not be created on repeat runs — the key-material test guarantees idempotency.
- **Idempotency/retry:** running `setup` then `headless-setup` then `setup` again, in any order, must converge on one line per distinct key and must never drop a line.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the append fails, `allowed_signers` keeps its prior content; `cmd_setup` should still return non-zero rather than printing OK.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `cmd_setup` in `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh`
- **Current line count:** 64 lines (`:178-241`); threshold is 100
- **Estimated growth:** +4 lines
- **Projected post-change:** ~68 lines (68% of threshold)
- **Action required:** None. `cmd_headless_setup` (`:253-335`, 83 lines) is closer to the limit — if step 3 adds more than ~10 lines, extract the allowed_signers reconciliation into a shared helper used by both functions.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** `shellcheck` covers the edited shell in both functions; the test file proves the ordering defect, the rotation-preservation guarantee, and idempotency on repeat runs; `linters-local.sh --changed` covers formatting and repo-wide shell policy for the two changed files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — two files, no shared contract, no root tooling, no release infrastructure.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** Do not change `gpg.format`, `commit.gpgsign`, `tag.gpgsign`, or `user.signingkey` selection. Do not make `cmd_setup` point `user.signingkey` at the headless key — `cmd_headless_setup:282-284` and `cmd_check` deliberately require the two to differ. Do not touch the ssh-agent lifecycle beyond the guidance strings in step 4.

**AI brief owner:** interactive session that filed this issue.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `headless-setup` followed by `setup`, `~/.ssh/allowed_signers` contains both the headless key and the key named by `user.signingkey`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `cmd_setup` no longer gates the append on principal presence alone.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "grep -q \"\\$git_email\" \"\\$ALLOWED_SIGNERS_FILE\""
    path: ".agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] Refreshing the headless key does not remove other principals' lines for the same email (negative guarantee, covered by the second test case).

- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh` reports zero violations.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh"
  ```

- [ ] The `agent-start` next-steps text no longer presents a shell-profile or cron hook as required.

- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`).

## Context & Decisions

- Matching on key material rather than principal was chosen because OpenSSH's `allowed_signers` is one line per key per principal, so multiple keys for one email are the expected steady state once both an interactive and a headless signing identity exist.
- Pointing `user.signingkey` at the headless key was ruled out: the key is passphrase-less, so any local process could sign as the user, and `cmd_headless_setup:282-284` plus `cmd_check` explicitly guard against it.
- `services.envfs` / `/usr/bin` symlinks were considered and rejected as unrelated: `reference/platform-support.md:75-79` states NixOS without envfs is supported and tools resolve through PATH, so no distro-specific host change belongs in this fix.
- The stale `agent-start` guidance is included because it is the same file, the same feature, and one line — not because it shares a root cause.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:212-229` — defective `cmd_setup` allowed_signers block
- `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:290-317` — correct two-stage pattern to model on, plus the over-broad replace
- `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:330-333` — stale agent-start guidance
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh:1-60` — sandbox harness: `TEST_HOME`, fake `git` and `ssh-add` on PATH
- `.agents/reference/git-signing.md:47-65` — documented agent self-heal behaviour that the guidance must match

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Blocks:** reliable local `git log --show-signature` verification for users who configure both signing identities
- **External:** none

title: pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd: log which probe failed when systemd backend is reported unavailable
body:
## What

`_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh` (lines 220-232) returns 1 from six different probes and discards each probe's reason. The only line reaching `pulse.log` is:

```
[dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: selected systemd backend unavailable for #NNN; detached fallback suppressed
```

The probes are an `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BACKEND=detached` override, `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SYSTEMD_WORKER_SERVICE=1`, a non-Linux `uname`, missing `systemd-run`, missing `systemctl`, and a failed `systemctl --user show --property=Version`. The manager probe also redirects its stderr to `/dev/null`, so messages such as `Failed to connect to bus` or a D-Bus timeout are lost. The GH#36390 error text says "see preceding dispatch_worker_launch lines for the backend cause", but no preceding line carries a cause.

## Why

A Linux runner (systemd 255, aidevops v3.39.131) tripped the supervisor circuit breaker with `worker_spawn_failed`. Seven consecutive launches for framework tasks #37046-#37052 all logged the line above within about 3 minutes, and the breaker tripped at 2026-11-07T09:58:06Z. Hundreds of earlier and later launches on the same runner succeeded through `systemd-run`. The probe passed again within minutes and returned in 8 ms. Nothing has recurred since: the current pulse log has 43 successful launches and 0 failures.

The host was heavily loaded at the time (load average about 46). The user manager had also just SIGKILLed the pulse service's control group after `TimeoutStartSec` (09:51:53Z). A slow or busy user manager is therefore the likely cause, but the runner's logs cannot confirm it, so the investigation had to end without a proven root cause. Operators get a breaker trip with no actionable cause.

## How

- Edit `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`: make `_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` record which probe failed. For example, set a `_DLW_SYSTEMD_UNAVAILABLE_REASON` value such as `env_detached`, `env_skip`, `not_linux`, `missing_systemd_run`, `missing_systemctl` or `manager_probe_failed rc=N stderr=<first line, sanitized>`.
- Include that reason in the existing `selected systemd backend unavailable` log line in `_dlw_launch_systemd_worker` (around line 461). Also record whether `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` were set as booleans, never their values.
- Optional, if the reason confirms slowness: bound the manager probe, for example `systemctl --user --timeout=...` or a short retry, so one slow D-Bus reply under load does not fail the whole launch. Keep the GH#36390 detached-fallback suppression unchanged.
- Reference pattern: `_dlw_handle_systemd_launch_failure` already writes a `classification=` line for post-submission failures. Mirror that for the pre-submission probe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-spawn-fail-fast.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-spawn-fail-fast.sh` (it already covers `worker_spawn_failed`). Stub `systemctl` to exit non-zero with a stderr message, then assert the log line carries `manager_probe_failed` and the sanitized message. Add one case for `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BACKEND=detached`.

title: Contribution watch marks new external replies notified without showing them; inbox lists 173 stale threads
body:
## What happens

Contribution watch notices new replies, but the owner never sees them, and the inbox it does show is mostly noise.

1. **Detected replies are swallowed.** `_scan_alert_item` (`.agents/scripts/contribution-watch-helper.sh:588-613`) sets `last_notified` to the item's `updated` time as soon as a scheduled scan sees it. Nothing human-facing follows:
   - the scan prints only to `~/.aidevops/logs/contribution-watch.log`;
   - the macOS notification is commented out (`:873-878`);
   - the pulse receives only a count and is told not to read bodies (`pulse-prefetch-secondary.sh:266-278`);
   - the session-start check counts only items with `last_any_comment > last_notified` (`aidevops-update-check.sh:466-471`), so it excludes every item the background scan has already flagged.
2. **The "need reply" list is noise.** `aidevops contributions` lists 173 of 199 tracked items as needing a reply, including:
   - merged or closed threads;
   - threads where the owner posted last and only a bot followed;
   - threads where the owner's own comment is not recorded in `last_our_comment`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `jq -r '.items["block/buzz-app#2432"] | [.last_any_comment, .last_our_comment, .last_notified] | @tsv' ~/.aidevops/cache/contribution-watch.json`

**Actual output:** (2026-11-08)

```
2026-11-08T02:42:06Z	2026-11-07T02:33:28Z	2026-11-08T02:42:06Z
```

An external maintainer's reply at 02:41Z was flagged by the 02:54Z scheduled scan (`actionable=1` in the log) and marked notified at once. The session-start count (same `jq` filter as `aidevops-update-check.sh:466-471`) returns 9 items, all from 2019 to 2026-09. Neither this reply nor the 2026-11-07T23:28Z activity on another watched PR is among them. The owner found both replies by hand.

**Noise examples from `aidevops contributions` on the same day:**

- `block/buzz#9191`: PR is MERGED. Last human comment is the owner's (2026-11-06T17:47:10Z), but `last_our_comment` is empty.
- `block/buzz#5440`: the owner commented at 20:09:30Z, then `github-actions[bot]` at 20:09:36Z. Listed as needing reply.
- `10up/distributor#294`: last activity 2019-06-24. Listed as needing reply.
- Merged PRs on the owner's own non-pulse repos, e.g. `marcusquinn/jerseytides.com#1`.

**Expected:** a new human reply on a watched external thread stays visible to the owner until the owner replies or dismisses it. The inbox lists only open threads where a non-bot human other than the owner posted last.

## Approach

- Split "alerted by a background scan" from "seen by the owner". Keep a separate `last_seen` (or an unseen queue) that only an interactive surface advances: session start, `aidevops contributions`, or an explicit dismiss. Base the session-start count on that, so background detection no longer hides items.
- Inbox filter: skip bot authors (`[bot]` suffix, `github-actions`) when computing `last_any_comment`. Skip MERGED/CLOSED threads unless a human replied after they closed. Backfill `last_our_comment` from the thread's own comments when it is empty.
- Show the newest items first in `aidevops contributions`, capped at about 20, with the total count.
- Optional: a quiet notification channel (no sound) or a Buzz post through the buzz-aidevops plugin later. Out of scope here unless trivial.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/contribution-watch-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/` (extend the existing contribution-watch test if one exists; otherwise verify with the fixture commands below)

## Verification

- Fixture state with one fresh human reply, one bot-only follow-up, one merged thread and one thread where the owner posted last. After a scan, the session-start count is 1 and `aidevops contributions` lists only the fresh reply.
- After `aidevops contributions` shows it (or after a dismiss), the next session-start count is 0.
- `shellcheck` clean on both scripts.

title: full-loop-helper merge: gh-closing-reference-lib.sh calls undefined _gh_extract_repo_from_args
body:
## What happens

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo>` (aidevops v3.39.127) prints, after a successful squash merge:

```
.../scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh: line 201: _gh_extract_repo_from_args: command not found
```

Seen on two consecutive merges in one interactive session (a bugfix PR and a release PR). The merge, canonical sync and closing-issue reconciliation still report success (`CLOSING_ISSUE_RECONCILIATION=converged`).

## Cause (from reading the deployed scripts)

- `gh-closing-reference-lib.sh` L191–201: `_gh_validate_pr_worker_identity()` calls `_gh_extract_repo_from_args "$@"` when `_GH_PR_IDENTITY_ORIGIN` is `edit`.
- `_gh_extract_repo_from_args` is defined in `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` L135, which the merge helper's PR-edit path does not appear to source before this library runs.
- Result: `repo` is empty for that check, so the worker-identity validation of a PR body edit silently runs without a repo.

## Suggested fix

Source `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` (or move `_gh_extract_repo_from_args` into a shared lib both use) wherever `gh-closing-reference-lib.sh` is sourced, or guard the call with `declare -F _gh_extract_repo_from_args` and fail closed with a clear message.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh` (L201)
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh` (L135)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (merge path, the PR body edit after merge)

## Verification

Run `full-loop-helper.sh merge` on a PR whose body the helper edits after merge: no `command not found` on stderr, and the worker-identity check receives the repo.

title: fix(lifecycle): managed takeover bursts per-item open-PR lookups; gh governor defers all (exit 75)
body:
## What

The observation-era managed takeover (GH#37034, merged in #37036, shipped in v3.39.135) runs `open_pull_requests(slug)` once per modern worktree for the precheck in `take_over_managed`. It runs it again for each eligible item's journaled plan and again for the pre-removal refresh. Each lookup is `gh api repos/{slug}` plus a paginated `gh api repos/{slug}/pulls`, so one pass makes roughly 2 × N calls just for prechecks, all in a quick burst.

On a shared Linux runner with the pulse's `gh` governor (`.agents/scripts/gh` → `gh-transport-governor.py`), that burst is deferred with exit 75. Every deferred item is retained with the generic reason `CalledProcessError`, so the takeover retires nothing.

## Evidence (shared host, v3.39.135, 2026-11-08 ~04:10Z)

- The latest `Observation-era cleanup:` passes show `{"reason":"CalledProcessError","count":51}` (runner A) and `count 34` then `63` (runner B). Before v3.39.135 these counts were 0–6.
- In `Cleanup diagnostics`, the subprocess failures are 67 (runner A) and 93 (runner B) rows of `ownership=managed-by-current-cleanup operation=subprocess returncode=75`.
- Runner B's token still had 4,427/5,000 core calls left, so this is the governor's local pacing/admission, not quota exhaustion. Runner A's token had about 435/5,000 left, and the same burst competes with dispatch workers for it.
- The target repo has 34 open PRs (one page), so the per-item lookup returns the same data every time within a pass.
- Across both runners, `Observation-era cleanup: retired=0` on those passes.

## How

Files:
- EDIT `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`. In `take_over_managed` (about line 189) and the preview branch of `process_reconstructible` (about line 315), use a pass-scoped memo per slug instead of calling `open_pull_requests` for every item. Keep the pre-removal `prefetched_pull_requests` lookup fresh, one per actual removal, so removal authority still rests on current GitHub state (GH#36851/GH#36921 contracts).
- EDIT `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_runner.py` or `legacy_options.py` to own the per-pass memo. Reference pattern: `OpenPullRequestCache` in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/pull_requests.py:91`, already used by admission cleanup in `cleanup.py:267`. A failed lookup is memoised as "unavailable" for the rest of the pass, so one deferral does not trigger N more calls.
- EDIT `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_options.py` (`retained_outcome`) or `cleanup_failure.py`. Report a governor deferral (exit 75 from a `gh` lookup) as a concrete reason such as `pull-request-state-unavailable`, not `CalledProcessError`.
- Tests: extend `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reconstructible.py` (managed takeover cases). Assert one lookup per slug per pass for prechecks, a fresh lookup before each removal, and that an exit-75 lookup yields the concrete retained reason without further lookups that pass.

Safety: a failed or unavailable lookup must still hold, never prove absence. Keep every existing guard: clean including untracked, HEAD on a remote ref, no open PR, idle /proc, unlocked, closed admission, non-forced removal, branch kept.

## Acceptance

- In a pass over N managed candidates for one slug, the precheck makes at most one `open_pull_requests` lookup per slug.
- Each actual removal still performs one fresh pre-removal lookup.
- A `gh` exit 75 is reported as `pull-request-state-unavailable` and stops further lookups for that slug in the pass.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -p 'test_reconstructible.py'` and `test_legacy_cleanup.py` pass. Linux CI is authoritative for `/proc` tests.
- After release, runner logs show `CalledProcessError` retentions near zero and nonzero managed takeover retirements.
